13	# ScrollArea
14	
15	`ScrollArea` wraps a scrollable region and replaces native OS scrollbars with fully styleable custom scrollbars. The viewport still uses native scroll for accessibility and performance; the custom scrollbars are overlaid and synchronised. Supports vertical, horizontal, and both axes; four visibility modes (`Always`, `Auto`, `Hover`, `Scroll`); drag-to-scroll via thumb dragging; page-scroll via track clicks; and RTL support.
16	
17	ScrollArea MUST preserve native keyboard scrolling (arrow keys, Page Up/Down, Home/End). Custom scrollbar styling is purely visual.

201	### 1.5 Thumb Metrics Computation
202	
203	```rust
204	/// Compute thumb `(size, position)` for one axis.
205	///
206	/// - `viewport_size`: visible extent of the viewport (px)
207	/// - `content_size`: total scrollable content extent (px)
208	/// - `scroll_pos`: current scroll offset (px)
209	/// - `track_size`: length of the scrollbar track (px)
210	/// - `min_thumb_size`: floor for thumb length (px)
211	///
212	/// Returns `(thumb_size, thumb_offset)`.
213	pub fn compute_thumb_metrics(
214	    viewport_size: f64,
215	    content_size: f64,
216	    scroll_pos: f64,
217	    track_size: f64,
218	    min_thumb_size: f64,
219	) -> (f64, f64) {
220	    if content_size <= viewport_size {
221	        return (track_size, 0.0);
222	    }
223	    let ratio = viewport_size / content_size;
224	    let thumb_size = (ratio * track_size).max(min_thumb_size).min(track_size);
225	    let scrollable_content = content_size - viewport_size;
226	    let scrollable_track = track_size - thumb_size;
227	    let thumb_pos = if scrollable_content > 0.0 {
228	        (scroll_pos / scrollable_content) * scrollable_track
229	    } else {
230	        0.0
231	    };
232	    (thumb_size, thumb_pos)
233	}
234	
235	/// Inverse: given a thumb position, compute the scroll position.
236	pub fn thumb_pos_to_scroll(
237	    thumb_pos: f64,
238	    track_size: f64,
239	    thumb_size: f64,
240	    content_size: f64,
241	    viewport_size: f64,
242	) -> f64 {
243	    let scrollable_track = track_size - thumb_size;
244	    let scrollable_content = content_size - viewport_size;
245	    if scrollable_track <= 0.0 { return 0.0; }
246	    (thumb_pos / scrollable_track) * scrollable_content
247	}
248	```

252	```rust
253	pub struct Machine;
254	
255	impl ars_core::Machine for Machine {
256	    type State = State;
257	    type Event = Event;
258	    type Context = Context;
259	    type Props = Props;
260	    type Messages = Messages;
261	    type Api<'a> = Api<'a>;
262	
263	    fn init(props: &Self::Props, env: &Env, messages: &Self::Messages) -> (Self::State, Self::Context) {
264	        let locale = env.locale.clone();
265	        let messages = messages.clone();
266	        let mut ctx = Context {
267	            scroll_x: 0.0, scroll_y: 0.0,
268	            viewport_width: 0.0, viewport_height: 0.0,
269	            content_width: 0.0, content_height: 0.0,
270	            scrollbar_x_visible: false, scrollbar_y_visible: false,
271	            hovering_scrollbar: false,
272	            scrollbar_visibility: props.scrollbar_visibility,
273	            min_thumb_size: props.min_thumb_size.unwrap_or(20.0),
274	            hide_delay_ms: props.hide_delay_ms.unwrap_or(1200),
275	            scrollbar_cross_size: 0.0,
276	            drag_start_pointer_pos: 0.0,
277	            drag_start_thumb_pos: 0.0,
278	            drag_start_scroll_pos: 0.0,
279	            drag_axis: None,
280	            ids: ComponentIds::from_id(&props.id),
281	            dir: props.dir.unwrap_or(Direction::Ltr),
282	            locale,
283	            messages,
284	        };
285	        ctx.update_visibility();
286	        (State::Idle, ctx)
287	    }
288	
289	    fn transition(
290	        state: &Self::State,
291	        event: &Self::Event,
292	        ctx: &Self::Context,
293	        props: &Self::Props,
294	    ) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Self>> {
295	        match event {
296	            Event::Resize { viewport_width, viewport_height, content_width, content_height } => {
297	                let (vw, vh, cw, ch) = (*viewport_width, *viewport_height, *content_width, *content_height);
298	                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| {
299	                    ctx.viewport_width = vw; ctx.viewport_height = vh;
300	                    ctx.content_width = cw; ctx.content_height = ch;
301	                    ctx.update_visibility();
302	                }))
303	            }
304	
305	            Event::Scroll { x, y } => {
306	                let (sx, sy) = (*x, *y);
307	                if ctx.scrollbar_visibility == ScrollbarVisibility::Scroll {
308	                    let delay = ctx.hide_delay_ms;
309	                    Some(TransitionPlan::to(State::ScrollActive).apply(move |ctx| {
310	                        ctx.scroll_x = sx; ctx.scroll_y = sy;
311	                        ctx.scrollbar_x_visible = ctx.has_overflow_x();
312	                        ctx.scrollbar_y_visible = ctx.has_overflow_y();
313	                    }).with_named_effect("auto-hide-scrollbar", move |_ctx, _props, send| {
314	                        let platform = use_platform_effects();
315	                        let handle = platform.set_timeout(delay, Box::new(move || send(Event::HideTimeout)));
316	                        let pc = platform.clone();
317	                        Box::new(move || pc.clear_timeout(handle))
318	                    }))
319	                } else {
320	                    Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| {
321	                        ctx.scroll_x = sx; ctx.scroll_y = sy;
322	                    }))
323	                }
324	            }
325	
326	            Event::MouseEnter => {
327	                if ctx.scrollbar_visibility == ScrollbarVisibility::Hover {
328	                    Some(TransitionPlan::to(State::Hovering).apply(|ctx| {
329	                        ctx.scrollbar_x_visible = ctx.has_overflow_x();
330	                        ctx.scrollbar_y_visible = ctx.has_overflow_y();
331	                    }))
332	                } else { None }
333	            }
334	
335	            Event::MouseLeave => {
336	                if ctx.scrollbar_visibility == ScrollbarVisibility::Hover && !ctx.hovering_scrollbar {
337	                    Some(TransitionPlan::to(State::Idle).apply(|ctx| {
338	                        ctx.scrollbar_x_visible = false; ctx.scrollbar_y_visible = false;
339	                    }))
340	                } else { None }
341	            }
342	
343	            Event::MouseEnterScrollbar => Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(|ctx| { ctx.hovering_scrollbar = true; })),
344	            Event::MouseLeaveScrollbar => Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(|ctx| { ctx.hovering_scrollbar = false; })),
345	
346	            Event::HideTimeout => {
347	                if *state != State::ThumbDragging {
348	                    Some(TransitionPlan::to(State::Idle).apply(|ctx| {
349	                        ctx.scrollbar_x_visible = false; ctx.scrollbar_y_visible = false;
350	                    }))
351	                } else { None }
352	            }
353	
354	            Event::ThumbDragStart { pos, axis } => {
355	                let (p, a) = (*pos, *axis);
356	                let scroll_pos = match a { Axis::X => ctx.scroll_x, Axis::Y => ctx.scroll_y };
357	                let (viewport_size, content_size, track_size) = axis_metrics(ctx, a);
358	                let min_thumb = ctx.min_thumb_size;
359	                Some(TransitionPlan::to(State::ThumbDragging).apply(move |ctx| {
360	                    ctx.drag_start_pointer_pos = p;
361	                    let (_, current_thumb_pos) = compute_thumb_metrics(
362	                        viewport_size, content_size, scroll_pos, track_size, min_thumb,
363	                    );
364	                    ctx.drag_start_thumb_pos = current_thumb_pos;
365	                    ctx.drag_start_scroll_pos = scroll_pos;
366	                    ctx.drag_axis = Some(a);
367	                }))
368	            }
369	
370	            Event::ThumbDragMove { pos } => {
371	                if *state != State::ThumbDragging { return None; }
372	                let axis = ctx.drag_axis?;
373	                let p = *pos;
374	                let (drag_start_pointer, drag_start_thumb, drag_scroll, min_thumb) =
375	                    (ctx.drag_start_pointer_pos, ctx.drag_start_thumb_pos, ctx.drag_start_scroll_pos, ctx.min_thumb_size);
376	                let (viewport_size, content_size, track_size) = axis_metrics(ctx, axis);
377	                let delta = p - drag_start_pointer;
378	                let (thumb_size, _) = compute_thumb_metrics(viewport_size, content_size, drag_scroll, track_size, min_thumb);
379	                let new_thumb_pos = (drag_start_thumb + delta).max(0.0);
380	                let new_scroll = thumb_pos_to_scroll(new_thumb_pos, track_size, thumb_size, content_size, viewport_size);
381	                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| {
382	                    match axis { Axis::X => ctx.scroll_x = new_scroll, Axis::Y => ctx.scroll_y = new_scroll }
383	                }))
384	            }
385	
386	            Event::ThumbDragEnd => {
387	                Some(TransitionPlan::to(State::Idle).apply(|ctx| { ctx.drag_axis = None; }))
388	            }
389	
390	            Event::TrackClick { pos, axis } => {
391	                let (a, p) = (*axis, *pos);
392	                let scroll_pos = match a { Axis::X => ctx.scroll_x, Axis::Y => ctx.scroll_y };
393	                let (viewport_size, content_size, track_size) = axis_metrics(ctx, a);
394	                let (thumb_size, thumb_pos) = compute_thumb_metrics(viewport_size, content_size, scroll_pos, track_size, ctx.min_thumb_size);
395	                let new_scroll = if p < thumb_pos {
396	                    (scroll_pos - viewport_size).max(0.0)
397	                } else if p > thumb_pos + thumb_size {
398	                    (scroll_pos + viewport_size).min(content_size - viewport_size)
399	                } else { scroll_pos };
400	                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| {
401	                    match a { Axis::X => ctx.scroll_x = new_scroll, Axis::Y => ctx.scroll_y = new_scroll }
402	                }))
403	            }
404	        }
405	    }
406	
407	    fn connect<'a>(
408	        state: &'a State, ctx: &'a Context, props: &'a Props, send: &'a dyn Fn(Event),
409	    ) -> Api<'a> {
410	        Api { state, ctx, props, send }
411	    }
412	}
413	
414	/// Helper: get (viewport_size, content_size, track_size) for an axis,
415	/// accounting for the cross-axis scrollbar's CornerSquare gap.
416	fn axis_metrics(ctx: &Context, axis: Axis) -> (f64, f64, f64) {
417	    match axis {
418	        Axis::X => {
419	            let cross = if ctx.scrollbar_y_visible { ctx.scrollbar_cross_size } else { 0.0 };
420	            (ctx.viewport_width, ctx.content_width, ctx.viewport_width - cross)
421	        }
422	        Axis::Y => {
423	            let cross = if ctx.scrollbar_x_visible { ctx.scrollbar_cross_size } else { 0.0 };
424	            (ctx.viewport_height, ctx.content_height, ctx.viewport_height - cross)
425	        }
426	    }
427	}

431	
432	```rust
433	#[derive(ComponentPart)]
434	#[scope = "scroll-area"]
435	pub enum Part {
436	    Root,
437	    Viewport,
438	    Content,
439	    ScrollbarY,
440	    ThumbY,
441	    ScrollbarX,
442	    ThumbX,
443	    CornerSquare,
444	}
445	
446	pub struct Api<'a> {
447	    state: &'a State,
448	    ctx: &'a Context,
449	    props: &'a Props,
450	    send: &'a dyn Fn(Event),
451	}
452	
453	impl<'a> Api<'a> {
454	    /// Whether the viewport is scrolled to the top edge.
455	    pub fn is_at_top(&self) -> bool { self.ctx.scroll_y <= 0.0 }
456	
457	    /// Whether the viewport is scrolled to the bottom edge.
458	    pub fn is_at_bottom(&self) -> bool {
459	        self.ctx.scroll_y >= (self.ctx.content_height - self.ctx.viewport_height).max(0.0)
460	    }
461	
462	    /// Whether the viewport is scrolled to the left edge.
463	    pub fn is_at_left(&self) -> bool { self.ctx.scroll_x <= 0.0 }
464	
465	    /// Whether the viewport is scrolled to the right edge.
466	    pub fn is_at_right(&self) -> bool {
467	        self.ctx.scroll_x >= (self.ctx.content_width - self.ctx.viewport_width).max(0.0)
468	    }
469	
470	    /// Current scroll progress as `(x, y)` in the range `0.0..=1.0`.
471	    pub fn scroll_progress(&self) -> (f64, f64) {
472	        let px = if self.ctx.content_width > self.ctx.viewport_width {
473	            self.ctx.scroll_x / (self.ctx.content_width - self.ctx.viewport_width)
474	        } else { 0.0 };
475	        let py = if self.ctx.content_height > self.ctx.viewport_height {
476	            self.ctx.scroll_y / (self.ctx.content_height - self.ctx.viewport_height)
477	        } else { 0.0 };
478	        (px.clamp(0.0, 1.0), py.clamp(0.0, 1.0))
479	    }
480	
481	    pub fn root_attrs(&self) -> AttrMap {
482	        let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();
483	        let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = Part::Root.data_attrs();
484	        attrs.set(scope_attr, scope_val);
485	        attrs.set(part_attr, part_val);
486	        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-state"), match self.state {
487	            State::Idle => "idle",
488	            State::Hovering => "hovering",
489	            State::ScrollActive => "scroll-active",
490	            State::ThumbDragging => "thumb-dragging",
491	        });
492	        attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-overflow-x"), self.ctx.has_overflow_x());
493	        attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-overflow-y"), self.ctx.has_overflow_y());
494	        if self.ctx.dir == Direction::Rtl {
495	            attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-dir"), "rtl");
496	        }
497	        attrs
498	    }
499	
500	    pub fn viewport_attrs(&self) -> AttrMap {
501	        let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();
502	        let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = Part::Viewport.data_attrs();
503	        attrs.set(scope_attr, scope_val);
504	        attrs.set(part_attr, part_val);
505	        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Role, "region");
506	        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::TabIndex, "0");
507	        if let Some(label) = &self.props.aria_label {
508	            attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Label), label.as_str());
509	        } else {
510	            attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Label), (self.ctx.messages.viewport_label)(&self.ctx.locale));
511	        }
512	        attrs
513	    }

600	
601	## 2. Anatomy
602	
603	```text
604	ScrollArea
605	├── Root           <div>   data-ars-state data-ars-overflow-x data-ars-overflow-y
606	│   ├── Viewport   <div>   role="region" tabindex="0" (native scroll)
607	│   │   └── Content <div>  (inner content wrapper)
608	│   ├── ScrollbarY <div>   role="none" (vertical track)
609	│   │   └── ThumbY <div>   role="none" (vertical thumb)
610	│   ├── ScrollbarX <div>   role="none" (horizontal track)
611	│   │   └── ThumbX <div>   role="none" (horizontal thumb)
612	│   └── CornerSquare <div> role="none" (gap filler when both axes)
613	```
614	
615	| Part         | Element | Key Attributes                                      |
616	| ------------ | ------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
617	| Root         | `<div>` | `data-ars-state`, `data-ars-overflow-x/y`           |
618	| Viewport     | `<div>` | `role="region"`, `tabindex="0"`, `aria-label`       |
619	| Content      | `<div>` | Inner content wrapper                               |
620	| ScrollbarY   | `<div>` | `role="none"`, `data-ars-visible`                   |
621	| ThumbY       | `<div>` | `role="none"`, sized/positioned by thumb metrics    |
622	| ScrollbarX   | `<div>` | `role="none"`, `data-ars-visible`                   |
623	| ThumbX       | `<div>` | `role="none"`, sized/positioned by thumb metrics    |
624	| CornerSquare | `<div>` | `role="none"`, visible when both scrollbars present |
625	
626	## 3. Accessibility
627	
628	### 3.1 ARIA Roles, States, and Properties
629	
630	| Element           | Attribute    | Value                                                   |
631	| ----------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------- |
632	| Viewport          | `role`       | `"region"`                                              |
633	| Viewport          | `aria-label` | Consumer-provided label                                 |
634	| Viewport          | `tabindex`   | `"0"` (focusable for keyboard scrolling)                |
635	| Scrollbars/Thumbs | `role`       | `"none"` (decorative; screen readers use native scroll) |
636	
637	- Custom scrollbar tracks and thumbs are decorative duplicates of the native scroll mechanism. They use `role="none"` (ARIA 1.2) to be excluded from the accessibility tree.
638	- Keyboard users scroll the viewport using standard browser key behaviours (arrow keys, Page Up/Down, Space).
639	- No `tabindex` is placed on scrollbar elements.
640	
641	## 4. Internationalization
642	
643	### 4.1 Messages
644	
645	```rust
646	#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
647	pub struct Messages {
648	    pub viewport_label: MessageFn<dyn Fn(&Locale) -> String + Send + Sync>,
649	}
650	
651	impl Default for Messages {
652	    fn default() -> Self {
653	        Self { viewport_label: MessageFn::static_str("Scrollable content") }
654	    }
655	}
656	
657	impl ComponentMessages for Messages {}
658	```
659	
660	### 4.2 RTL Support
661	
662	**Vertical scrollbar position:** In `dir="rtl"`, `data-ars-dir="rtl"` is set on Root. CSS targets this to move the vertical scrollbar to the left side:
663	
664	```css
665	[data-ars-dir="rtl"] [data-ars-part="scrollbar-y"] {
666	    right: auto;
667	    left: 0;
668	}
669	```
670	
671	**Horizontal scroll normalization:** RTL browsers use different `scrollLeft` conventions. The machine normalizes to a 0-to-positive range:
672	
673	```rust
674	/// Normalizes `scrollLeft` across browser RTL conventions.
675	/// - Standard (Chrome, Firefox >= 112): negative values, 0 at left edge
676	/// - Legacy Firefox (< 112): negative values, 0 at right edge
677	/// - Safari/WebKit: positive values, 0 at right edge
678	///
679	/// Returns normalized value in range [0, scrollWidth - clientWidth].
680	fn normalize_scroll_left(raw: f64, scroll_width: f64, client_width: f64, is_rtl: bool) -> f64 {
681	    if !is_rtl {
682	        return raw;
683	    }
684	    // Detect convention by checking sign of scrollLeft at initial position
685	    // Modern standard: raw <= 0, normalize to positive range
686	    if raw <= 0.0 {
687	        raw.abs()
688	    } else {
689	        // Safari positive convention: already positive
690	        scroll_width - client_width - raw
691	    }
692	}
693	```
694	
695	## 5. Library Parity
696	
697	> Compared against: Ark UI (`ScrollArea`), Radix UI (`ScrollArea`).
698	
699	### 5.1 Props
700	
701	| Feature                   | ars-ui                           | Ark UI                  | Radix UI                | Notes                                            |
702	| ------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
703	| Scrollbar visibility mode | `scrollbar_visibility` (4 modes) | --                      | `type` (4 modes)        | Same semantics, different naming                 |
704	| Hide delay                | `hide_delay_ms`                  | --                      | `scrollHideDelay`       | Same feature                                     |
705	| Direction (RTL)           | `dir`                            | --                      | `dir`                   | Same feature                                     |
706	| CSP nonce                 | --                               | --                      | `nonce`                 | Adapter-level concern in ars-ui; not a core prop |
707	| Orientation               | `orientation`                    | Scrollbar `orientation` | Scrollbar `orientation` | ars-ui sets at Root; refs set per-scrollbar      |
708	| Min thumb size            | `min_thumb_size`                 | --                      | --                      | ars-ui addition                                  |
709	| Accessible label          | `aria_label`                     | --                      | --                      | ars-ui addition                                  |
710	
711	**Gaps:** None. `nonce` is handled at the adapter layer.
712	
713	### 5.2 Anatomy
714	
715	| Part                   | ars-ui         | Ark UI      | Radix UI    | Notes                               |
716	| ---------------------- | -------------- | ----------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------- |
717	| Root                   | `Root`         | `Root`      | `Root`      | --                                  |
718	| Viewport               | `Viewport`     | `Viewport`  | `Viewport`  | --                                  |
719	| Content                | `Content`      | `Content`   | --          | Radix nests content inside Viewport |
720	| Scrollbar (vertical)   | `ScrollbarY`   | `Scrollbar` | `Scrollbar` | ars-ui splits per-axis              |
721	| Scrollbar (horizontal) | `ScrollbarX`   | `Scrollbar` | `Scrollbar` | ars-ui splits per-axis              |
722	| Thumb (vertical)       | `ThumbY`       | `Thumb`     | `Thumb`     | ars-ui splits per-axis              |
723	| Thumb (horizontal)     | `ThumbX`       | `Thumb`     | `Thumb`     | ars-ui splits per-axis              |
724	| Corner                 | `CornerSquare` | `Corner`    | `Corner`    | Same feature                        |
725	
726	**Gaps:** None.
727	
728	### 5.3 Events
729	
730	| Callback        | ars-ui                    | Ark UI | Radix UI | Notes                |
731	| --------------- | ------------------------- | ------ | -------- | -------------------- |
732	| Scroll position | `Event::Scroll`           | --     | --       | State machine event  |
733	| Resize          | `Event::Resize`           | --     | --       | State machine event  |
734	| Thumb drag      | `ThumbDragStart/Move/End` | --     | --       | State machine events |
735	| Track click     | `Event::TrackClick`       | --     | --       | State machine event  |
736	
737	**Gaps:** None. Ark UI and Radix UI handle these internally without exposing callbacks.
738	
739	### 5.4 Features
740	
741	| Feature                   | ars-ui                                           | Ark UI                                           | Radix UI |
742	| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ | -------- |
743	| Custom scrollbar styling  | Yes                                              | Yes                                              | Yes      |
744	| Four visibility modes     | Yes                                              | --                                               | Yes      |
745	| Drag-to-scroll (thumb)    | Yes                                              | Yes                                              | Yes      |
746	| Track click (page scroll) | Yes                                              | Yes                                              | Yes      |
747	| RTL support               | Yes                                              | --                                               | Yes      |
748	| Scroll position queries   | `is_at_top/bottom/left/right`, `scroll_progress` | `isAtTop/Bottom/Left/Right`, `getScrollProgress` | --       |
749	| Scroll-to APIs            | --                                               | `scrollToEdge`, `scrollTo`                       | --       |
750	
751	**Gaps:** Ark UI exposes `scrollToEdge` and `scrollTo` imperative APIs. These are adapter-level operations (calling `element.scrollTo()`) rather than state machine concerns. Adapters can provide these as utility methods on the framework wrapper without core spec changes.
752	
753	### 5.5 Summary
754	
755	- **Overall:** Full parity.
756	- **Divergences:** ars-ui splits scrollbars into per-axis parts (`ScrollbarY`/`ScrollbarX`) instead of parameterized `Scrollbar(orientation)`. This is more explicit and avoids runtime orientation checks.
757	- **Recommended additions:** None.
758	
```

208	/// ARIA attributes are conveyed through `AttrMap` using `HtmlAttr::Aria(...)` variants,
209	/// as defined in `01-architecture.md` §3. There is no flat `AriaAttributes` struct;
210	/// all ARIA attributes are inserted into the component's `AttrMap` by the state machine's

216	/// attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::ValueNow), current.to_string());
217	/// attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::ValueMin), min.to_string());
218	/// attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::ValueMax), max.to_string());
219	/// attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Orientation), "horizontal");

### 3. Part Derive Macro and data_attrs() Usage

**The ComponentPart derive macro** with `#[scope = "..."]` generates the `data_attrs()` method.

**Example from splitter:**

```rust
#[derive(ComponentPart)]
#[scope = "splitter"]
pub enum Part {
    Root,
    Panel { index: usize },
    Handle { index: usize },
}
```

**Usage in Api methods:**

```rust
pub fn root_attrs(&self) -> AttrMap {
    let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();
    let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = Part::Root.data_attrs();
    
    attrs
        .set(scope_attr, scope_val)           // data-ars-scope="splitter"
        .set(part_attr, part_val)             // data-ars-part="root"
        .set(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-orientation"), "horizontal")
        .set(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-state"), "idle");
    
    attrs
}

pub fn panel_attrs(&self, index: usize) -> AttrMap {
    let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();
    let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = (Part::Panel { index }).data_attrs();
    
    attrs.set(scope_attr, scope_val).set(part_attr, part_val);
    // ... additional attrs
    attrs
}
```

The `data_attrs()` method returns a 2-tuple array of `(HtmlAttr, &'static str)`:
- `data-ars-scope="{scope}"` (from `#[scope = "..."]`)
- `data-ars-part="{part_variant_name}"` (auto-generated from enum variant)

    /// Left-right axis (used by Left/Right placements).
    Horizontal,
    /// Top-bottom axis (used by Top/Bottom placements).
    Vertical,
}
```

**Export chain:**
- Defined in `ars-dom/src/positioning/types.rs`
- Exported from `ars-dom/src/positioning/mod.rs` (likely)
- **NOT** re-exported in `ars-core` public API

**Usage note:** The ScrollArea spec uses `Axis::Horizontal` and `Axis::Vertical`, but `Axis` is **not** currently exported from `ars-core`. You'll need to either:
1. Import it directly from `ars-dom::positioning`, or
2. Define a local `Axis` enum in the scroll_area module matching the `ars-dom` definition, or
3. Use `Orientation` from `ars-core` (which has `Horizontal` and `Vertical` variants) as splitter does

**Current crate exports from ars-core:**
- `Direction` - `Ltr`, `Rtl`
- `Orientation` - from `ars_i18n`, has `Horizontal`, `Vertical`

## Summary for ScrollArea Implementation

When implementing `scroll_area/mod.rs` in `/crates/ars-components/src/layout/scroll_area/`, you should:

1. **Create a single `mod.rs` file** (not submodules) following the Splitter/Collapsible structure
2. **Expose it in** `/crates/ars-components/src/layout/mod.rs`:
   ```rust
   /// ScrollArea component machine.
   pub mod scroll_area;
   ```
3. **Use `Orientation`** (not `Axis`) from `ars_core` if matching Splitter patterns, or define a local `Axis` enum if the spec specifically requires it
4. **Derive `ComponentPart`** for the Part enum with `#[scope = "scroll-area"]` or `#[scope = "scroll_area"]`
5. **Structure sections** in order: imports → type aliases → State → Events → Context → Props → Messages → Machine → Part → Api → ConnectApi → tests
6. **No feature gates needed** — the module will be unconditionally included
7. **Export scrollbar Parts:** Root, Viewport, Content, Scrollbar(axis), Thumb(axis), Track(axis), CornerSquare per the spec

## Investigation Summary: Testing Conventions in ars-ui Workspace

I've thoroughly investigated the testing conventions in the ars-ui workspace for stateful components. Here are my findings:

### 1. Unit Test Organization (Inline Tests)

**Location:** Inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in each component's `mod.rs` file

**Example:** `/Users/ericson/Workspace/Rust/ars-ui.worktrees/impl-279/crates/ars-components/src/data_display/rating_group/mod.rs` (lines 1047-1764)

**Structure:**
- Tests are organized inline within the component's source file
- Each component module contains a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { ... }` block at the end
- The module imports necessary testing utilities and the component types
- Helper functions for common test operations are defined first

**Example Inline Test Structure (from rating_group/mod.rs):**
```rust
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use alloc::{string::String, vec::Vec};
    use core::{cell::RefCell, num::NonZero};
    use ars_core::{AttrMap, Env, Machine as _, Service};
    use ars_interactions::{KeyboardEventData, KeyboardKey};
    use insta::assert_snapshot;
    use super::*;

    const fn keyboard(key: KeyboardKey) -> KeyboardEventData { /* helper */ }

    fn service(props: Props) -> Service<Machine> {
        Service::<Machine>::new(props, &Env::default(), &Messages::default())
    }

    fn snapshot_attrs(attrs: &AttrMap) -> String {
        format!("{attrs:#?}")
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_name() { /* test body */ }
}
```

**Per-Component Test Split:** Each component (Avatar, Badge, RatingGroup, TagGroup, etc.) maintains its own tests inline. There is no separate per-component test file in `crates/ars-components/tests/` for unit tests.

### 3. Spec-Conformance Tests

**Location:** `/Users/ericson/Workspace/Rust/ars-ui.worktrees/impl-279/crates/ars-components/tests/spec_conformance/`

**Main File:** `/Users/ericson/Workspace/Rust/ars-ui.worktrees/impl-279/crates/ars-components/tests/spec_conformance.rs`

**Helper Module:** `/Users/ericson/Workspace/Rust/ars-ui.worktrees/impl-279/crates/ars-components/tests/spec_conformance/helper.rs`

**Purpose:** Asserts that a component's `Part` enum matches the anatomy table declared in the spec's §3 section.

**Helper Function** (`helper.rs`, lines 24-75):
```rust
pub(crate) fn assert_anatomy<P>(
    expected_scope: &'static str,
    expected_parts: &[(P, &'static str)]
)
where
    P: ComponentPart + core::fmt::Debug + PartialEq,
{
    assert_eq!(P::scope(), expected_scope, "Part::scope() must match spec §3 anatomy");
    let actual = P::all();
    let actual_names = actual.iter().map(ComponentPart::name).collect::<Vec<_>>();
    let expected_names = expected_parts.iter().map(|(_, name)| *name).collect::<Vec<_>>();
    assert_eq!(actual_names, expected_names, "Part::all() name list must equal spec §3 anatomy");
    // ... additional assertions
    assert_eq!(&P::ROOT, first_expected, "Part::ROOT (first variant) must equal first spec-declared part");
}
```

**Example Conformance Test** (from `data_display.rs`, lines 123-134):
```rust
#[test]
fn rating_group_anatomy_matches_spec() {
    assert_anatomy(
        "rating-group",
        &[
            (rating_group::Part::Root, "root"),
            (rating_group::Part::Label, "label"),
            (rating_group::Part::Control, "control"),
            (rating_group::Part::Item { index: 0 }, "item"),
            (rating_group::Part::HiddenInput, "hidden-input"),
        ],
    );
}
```

### 4. Proptest State Machine Tests

**Location:** `/Users/ericson/Workspace/Rust/ars-ui.worktrees/impl-279/crates/ars-components/tests/proptest_state_machines/`

**Common Helper:** `/Users/ericson/Workspace/Rust/ars-ui.worktrees/impl-279/crates/ars-components/tests/proptest_state_machines/common.rs` (lines 1-44)

**Helper Code:**
```rust
pub(super) fn proptest_config() -> Config {
    let cases = std::env::var("PROPTEST_CASES")
        .ok()
        .and_then(|v| v.parse().ok())
        .unwrap_or(1000);

    Config {
        cases,
        failure_persistence: Some(Box::new(FileFailurePersistence::Direct(
            "proptest-regressions/state-machines.txt",
        ))),
        ..Config::default()
    }
}
```

**Purpose:**
1. Reads `PROPTEST_CASES` env var for case count (default 1000, extended job uses 10,000)
2. Redirects failure seeds to single crate-root file at `proptest-regressions/state-machines.txt`

**Failure Persistence:** `/Users/ericson/Workspace/Rust/ars-ui.worktrees/impl-279/crates/ars-components/proptest-regressions/state-machines.txt` contains shrunk failure seeds committed to source control

**Example Proptest Block** (from `data_display.rs`, lines 390-428 - RatingGroup):
```rust
proptest! {
    #![proptest_config(super::super::common::proptest_config())]

    #[test]
    #[ignore = "proptest — nightly extended-proptest job"]
    fn proptest_rating_group_event_sequences_preserve_invariants(
        props in arb_props(),
        events in prop::collection::vec(arb_event(), 0..64),
    ) {
        let mut service = Service::<rating_group::Machine>::new(
            props,
            &Env::default(),
            &rating_group::Messages::default(),
        );

        let initial_value = *service.context().value.get();

        for event in events {
            drop(service.send(event));

            let ctx = service.context();
            let value = *ctx.value.get();
            let max = f64::from(ctx.count.get());

            prop_assert!(value.is_finite());
            prop_assert!((0.0..=max).contains(&value));

            if let Some(hovered) = ctx.hovered_value {
                prop_assert!(hovered.is_finite());
                prop_assert!((0.0..=max).contains(&hovered));
            }

            if ctx.disabled || ctx.readonly {
                prop_assert_eq!(value, initial_value);
            }
        }
    }
}
```

**Pattern Elements:**
- `#[test] #[ignore = "proptest — nightly extended-proptest job"]` - marked for nightly CI only
- `#![proptest_config(super::super::common::proptest_config())]` - centralizes config
- Arbitraries (`arb_props()`, `arb_event()`) define random input strategies
- Tests verify state machine invariants across arbitrary event sequences
- Use `prop_assert!` and `prop_assert_eq!` instead of regular assertions

### 5. Service and Machine API

**Service Location:** `/Users/ericson/Workspace/Rust/ars-ui.worktrees/impl-279/crates/ars-core/src/lib.rs` (lines 976-1403)

**Service::new()** (lines 1023-1041):
```rust
pub fn new(props: M::Props, env: &Env, messages: &M::Messages) -> Self {
    debug_assert!(!props.id().is_empty(), "Props::id must not be empty");
    let (state, context) = M::init(&props, env, messages);
    let initial_inputs = Some(InitialInputs {
        state: state.clone(),
        context: context.clone(),
    });
    Self {
        state,
        context,
        props,
        event_queue: VecDeque::new(),
        initial_inputs,
        unmounted: false,
    }
}
```

**Key Service Methods:**

1. **state()** (line 1080): Returns `&M::State` - read-only current state
2. **context()** (line 1086): Returns `&M::Context` - read-only current context
3. **send(event)** (line 1155): Queues and processes an event, returns `SendResult<M>`
4. **connect(send_fn)** (line 1386): Creates API snapshot with event handler closure
   ```rust
   pub fn connect<'a>(&'a self, send: &'a dyn Fn(M::Event)) -> M::Api<'a> {
       M::connect(&self.state, &self.context, &self.props, send)
   }
   ```
5. **set_props(new_props)** (line 1348): Updates props and triggers `M::on_props_changed()`
6. **set_state_for_test(state)** (line 1396): Test-only helper to force arbitrary state

**Typical Test Pattern:**
```rust
fn service(props: Props) -> Service<Machine> {
    Service::<Machine>::new(props, &Env::default(), &Messages::default())
}

// Test a sequence

drop(service.send(Event::Rate(4.0)));
assert_eq!(*service.context().value.get(), 2.0);  // Read context
assert_eq!(service.state(), &State::Idle);        // Read state

// Create API to test attributes
let api = service.connect(&|_| {});
assert_eq!(api.control_attrs().get(&HtmlAttr::Role), Some("radiogroup"));
```

### Summary Table

| Aspect | Location | Convention |
|--------|----------|------------|
| **Unit Tests** | `src/{category}/{component}/mod.rs` (inline `#[cfg(test)]`) | Inline tests per component |
| **Snapshots** | `src/{category}/{component}/snapshots/*.snap` | Insta format, stored per-component |
| **Snapshot Format** | Debug format via `format!("{attrs:#?}")` | Pretty-printed `AttrMap { attrs: [...], styles: [] }` |
| **Spec Conformance** | `tests/spec_conformance/` with `helper.rs` | Part enum vs spec anatomy table |
| **Proptest** | `tests/proptest_state_machines/` + common config | State machine invariant testing |
| **Config Centralization** | `tests/proptest_state_machines/common.rs` | Shared `proptest_config()` function |
| **Failure Persistence** | `proptest-regressions/state-machines.txt` | Single file, committed to source control |
| **Service Instantiation** | Test helper functions | `Service::new(props, &Env::default(), &Messages::default())` |
| **API Access** | `service.connect(&\|_\| {})` | Returns `M::Api<'a>` with part/attr methods |

---

This structure is ready for you to apply to the ScrollArea agnostic core using TDD. You can write inline tests with snapshots alongside the component, add spec conformance in the external test suite, and property-based tests for invariants.

//! Spec-conformance tests for `crates/ars-components/src/layout/*`.
//!
//! Each test pulls the expected anatomy from the corresponding component
//! spec's §2 anatomy table and asserts the impl's `Part` enum matches.

use ars_components::layout::{aspect_ratio, center, collapsible, frame, grid, splitter, stack};

use super::helper::assert_anatomy;

#[test]
fn aspect_ratio_anatomy_matches_spec() {
    assert_anatomy("aspect-ratio", &[(aspect_ratio::Part::Root, "root")]);
}

#[test]
fn frame_anatomy_matches_spec() {
    assert_anatomy(
        "frame",
        &[(frame::Part::Root, "root"), (frame::Part::Iframe, "iframe")],
    );
}

#[test]
fn stack_anatomy_matches_spec() {
    assert_anatomy("stack", &[(stack::Part::Root, "root")]);
}

#[test]
fn center_anatomy_matches_spec() {
    assert_anatomy("center", &[(center::Part::Root, "root")]);
}

#[test]
fn collapsible_anatomy_matches_spec() {
    assert_anatomy(
        "collapsible",
        &[
            (collapsible::Part::Root, "root"),
            (collapsible::Part::Trigger, "trigger"),
            (collapsible::Part::Indicator, "indicator"),
            (collapsible::Part::Content, "content"),
        ],
    );
}

#[test]
fn grid_anatomy_matches_spec() {
    assert_anatomy("grid", &[(grid::Part::Root, "root")]);
}

#[test]
fn splitter_anatomy_matches_spec() {
    assert_anatomy(
        "splitter",
        &[
            (splitter::Part::Root, "root"),
            (splitter::Part::Panel { index: 0 }, "panel"),
            (splitter::Part::Handle { index: 0 }, "handle"),
        ],
    );

//! Spec-conformance tests for ars-components.
//!
//! Each module asserts that a component's `Part` enum matches the
//! anatomy table declared in `spec/components/.../{component}.md` §3.
//! The test layer is intentionally tiny — it leans on the derive-generated
//! `Part::scope()`, `Part::all()`, and `Part::name()` to compare against a
//! hand-rolled allow-list of `(Part, expected-kebab-name)` pairs per
//! component.
//!
//! New components SHOULD add a sibling module here (or extend an existing
//! one) so any drift between the spec's declared parts and the impl is
//! caught at build time, not by a reviewer's eye.

The core must own all scrollbar math (thumb\nsize/position, visibility, drag state, orientation, attrs) and expose it through\na `Machine` + `ConnectApi`. All live DOM measurement, ResizeObserver/scroll\nlistener wiring, timers, and scroll reads/writes belong to the adapters and are\nout of scope here.\n\nSpec contract: `spec/components/layout/scroll-area.md` (tier: stateful) and\n`spec/shared/layout-shared-types.md`. The component is built in\n`crates/ars-components` (no `ars-dom` dependency — agnostic only).\n\n## Drift to resolve in this PR\n\nThe spec §1.6 code example is not directly buildable and embeds adapter concerns\nin the agnostic layer. ## Approved Plan (edited by user):
# Task #279 — Implement ScrollArea agnostic core

## Context

GitHub issue #279 (epic #226, Agnostic layout components, 5 pts) asks for the
framework-agnostic state machine for `ScrollArea`: a stateful component that
replaces native OS scrollbars with styleable custom scrollbars while preserving
native scroll/keyboard behaviour. The core must own all scrollbar math (thumb
size/position, visibility, drag state, orientation, attrs) and expose it through
a `Machine` + `ConnectApi`. All live DOM measurement, ResizeObserver/scroll
listener wiring, timers, and scroll reads/writes belong to the adapters and are
out of scope here.

Spec contract: `spec/components/layout/scroll-area.md` (tier: stateful) and
`spec/shared/layout-shared-types.md`. The component is built in
`crates/ars-components` (no `ars-dom` dependency — agnostic only).

## Drift to resolve in this PR

The spec §1.6 code example is not directly buildable and embeds adapter concerns
in the agnostic layer. The issue's "Element/ref handling note" + "Spec impact"
sections explicitly require pushing those to adapters. Two concrete fixes, both
landed in this PR (spec + code together):

1. **`Axis` is referenced but never defined.** `Event::ThumbDragStart`,
   `Event::TrackClick`, and `axis_metrics()` use `Axis::X`/`Axis::Y`, but no such
   type exists in any agnostic crate (`ars-dom`'s `Axis` is `Horizontal`/`Vertical`
   and lives in a wasm/DOM crate we must not depend on). **Fix:** define
   `pub enum Axis { X, Y }` in the `scroll_area` module and add its definition to
   spec §1.2.

2. **Auto-hide effect calls `use_platform_effects().set_timeout(...)` inside the
   machine.** Timers are a platform concern. The canonical workspace pattern
   (`overlay::tooltip` `Effect::OpenDelay`/`CloseDelay`, `rating_group`) is to emit
   a **named `Effect` intent** that the adapter owns; the core closure returns
   `no_cleanup()`. **Fix:** define `pub enum Effect { AutoHide }`, set
   `type Effect = Effect`, and replace the embedded `set_timeout` block with
   `.with_named_effect(Effect::AutoHide, |_ctx, _props, _send| no_cleanup())`. The
   adapter reads `ctx.hide_delay_ms`, runs the timer, and sends back
   `Event::HideTimeout`. Update spec §1.6 to match and add the adapter-contract note.

Note (no code change, flag only): `Context::scrollbar_cross_size` is used by
`axis_metrics()` but no event sets it (stays `0.0`). Implemented exactly as spec'd;
will be surfaced in the post-implementation audit as a possible follow-up.

Note: the issue's "Keyboard scroll intent (if focused)" is satisfied by native
scroll — spec §3 mandates `role="region"` + `tabindex="0"` on the viewport and
**no** keyboard events in the machine. The test asserts the viewport is focusable
(the mechanism that enables native keyboard scrolling), not a machine key handler.

## Implementation (TDD — tests first)

Single file `crates/ars-components/src/layout/scroll_area/mod.rs`, mirroring
`layout/splitter/mod.rs` and `layout/collapsible/mod.rs` structure. Section order:
imports → `Axis` → `State` → `Event` → `ScrollOrientation`/`ScrollbarVisibility` →
`Context` (+ `has_overflow_x/y`, `update_visibility`) → `ScrollDetail` → `Props`
(+ builder methods, `#[derive(..., ars_core::HasId)]`) → `Messages`
(+ `Default`, `ComponentMessages`) → `Effect` → free fns `compute_thumb_metrics`,
`thumb_pos_to_scroll`, `normalize_scroll_left`, `axis_metrics` → `Machine`
(`type Effect = Effect`, `init`/`transition`/`connect`) → `#[derive(ComponentPart)]
#[scope = "scroll-area"]` `Part` (8 variants: Root, Viewport, Content, ScrollbarY,
ThumbY, ScrollbarX, ThumbX, CornerSquare) → `Api` (query methods + per-part
`*_attrs()` + `on_*` event handlers) → `impl ConnectApi`.

Reused contracts (verified):
- `ars_core::{Machine, Service, TransitionPlan, ConnectApi, AttrMap, HtmlAttr,
  AriaAttr, ComponentIds, ComponentMessages, MessageFn, Env, no_cleanup}`,
  `ars_core::ComponentPart` derive.
- `ars_i18n::{Locale, Direction}` (re-exported via `ars_core`).
- `TransitionPlan::{to, context_only, apply, with_named_effect, cancel_effect}`;
  effect setup closure is `FnOnce(&Context, &Props, WeakSend<Event>) -> CleanupFn`.
- `MessageFn::static_str` for `viewport_label`.

Then declare it: add `pub mod scroll_area;` to `crates/ars-components/src/layout/mod.rs`.

## Tests (named in the issue)

Inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `scroll_area/mod.rs` (helper `service(props)` →
`Service::<Machine>::new(props, &Env::default(), &Messages::default())`,
`snapshot_attrs(attrs)` → `format!("{attrs:#?}")`):

- `compute_thumb_metrics`: thumb size proportional to viewport/content ratio,
  floored at `min_thumb_size`, capped at `track_size`; degenerate case
  (content ≤ viewport) returns `(track_size, 0.0)`.
- Thumb position tracks injected `scroll_pos`; `thumb_pos_to_scroll` is the inverse.
- Auto-hide: `Event::Scroll` in `Scroll` mode → `State::ScrollActive`, scrollbars
  visible, plan carries `Effect::AutoHide`; `Event::HideTimeout` → `Idle`, hidden;
  `HideTimeout` is a no-op while `ThumbDragging`.
- Horizontal + vertical tracks: `scrollbar_x_attrs`/`scrollbar_y_attrs` orientation
  + `data-ars-visible`; visibility per `ScrollOrientation`/`ScrollbarVisibility`.
- Drag: `ThumbDragStart`→`ThumbDragging` captures drag origin; `ThumbDragMove`
  produces correct `scroll_x`/`scroll_y` from injected pointer delta + track geom;
  `ThumbDragEnd`→`Idle`.
- `TrackClick`: page up/down jump intent above/below thumb; no-op on thumb.
- ConnectApi/ARIA: viewport `role="region"` + `tabindex="0"` + `aria-label`
  (custom prop and default-message fallback); scrollbars/thumbs/corner `role="none"`;
  root `data-ars-state`/`data-ars-overflow-x|y`/`data-ars-dir` (RTL).
- `normalize_scroll_left` across LTR / modern-RTL / Safari-RTL conventions.
- Query methods: `is_at_top/bottom/left/right`, `scroll_progress` clamps to 0..=1.
- Snapshot test (`insta::assert_snapshot!`) over every `*_attrs()` for each
  output-affecting branch (state, visibility mode, orientation, RTL). Fixtures in
  `crates/ars-components/src/layout/scroll_area/snapshots/`.

Harness wiring (single-file extensions):
- `crates/ars-components/tests/spec_conformance/layout.rs`: add
  `scroll_area_anatomy_matches_spec` asserting scope `"scroll-area"` + the 8 parts.
- `crates/ars-components/tests/proptest_state_machines/layout.rs`: add a
  `scroll_area` proptest (arb props + arb event sequence) asserting invariants:
  scroll offsets finite and clamped to `[0, content - viewport]`, visibility flags
  consistent with mode/overflow, `drag_axis` set iff `ThumbDragging`. Use
  `#![proptest_config(super::common::proptest_config())]` and
  `#[ignore = "proptest — nightly extended-proptest job"]`.

## Spec edits (same PR)

`spec/components/layout/scroll-area.md`:
- §1.2: add the `Axis` enum definition.
- §1.6: add `Effect` enum + `type Effect = Effect`; replace the `Scroll`-mode
  auto-hide `with_named_effect("auto-hide-scrollbar", … set_timeout …)` with the
  `Effect::AutoHide` + `no_cleanup()` intent and an adapter-contract note (adapter
  owns the `hide_delay_ms` timer and sends `Event::HideTimeout`). Drop the
  `use_platform_effects` import from the agnostic example.

## Verification

```bash
cargo test -p ars-components scroll_area
cargo insta test -p ars-components --unreferenced=reject   # review + accept .snap
cargo test -p ars-components --test spec_conformance layout
cargo test -p ars-components --test proptest_state_machines -- --ignored scroll_area
cargo fmt --all && cargo clippy -p ars-components --all-targets   # zero warnings
```

Then run `post-implementation-audit` (mandatory), present for review, and after
approval `cargo xci-fast`. Open PR targeting `main` with `Closes #279`; attach
`snapshot-reviewed` label (new `.snap` fixtures); run `waiting-for-codex-review`.

```

219	/// The machine for the `Collapsible` component.
220	#[derive(Debug)]
221	pub struct Machine;
222	
223	impl ars_core::Machine for Machine {
224	    type State = State;
225	    type Event = Event;
226	    type Context = Context;
227	    type Props = Props;
228	    type Messages = Messages;
229	    type Effect = NoEffect;
230	    type Api<'a> = Api<'a>;
231	
232	    fn init(
233	        props: &Self::Props,
234	        env: &Env,
235	        messages: &Self::Messages,
236	    ) -> (Self::State, Self::Context) {
237	        let initial_open = props.open.unwrap_or(props.default_open);
238	        let state = state_from_bool(initial_open);
239	
240	        let open = if let Some(value) = props.open {
241	            Bindable::controlled(value)
242	        } else {
243	            Bindable::uncontrolled(initial_open)
244	        };
245	
246	        (
247	            state,
248	            Context {
249	                open,
250	                disabled: props.disabled,
251	                focused: false,
252	                focus_visible: false,
253	                ids: ComponentIds::from_id(&props.id),
254	                collapsed_height: props.collapsed_height.clone(),
255	                collapsed_width: props.collapsed_width.clone(),
256	                locale: env.locale.clone(),
257	                messages: messages.clone(),
258	            },
259	        )
260	    }
261	
262	    fn transition(
263	        state: &Self::State,
264	        event: &Self::Event,
265	        ctx: &Self::Context,
266	        props: &Self::Props,
267	    ) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Self>> {
268	        match event {
269	            Event::Toggle if !ctx.disabled => open_transition(ctx, !ctx.open.get()),
270	
271	            Event::SetOpen(value) if !ctx.disabled => open_transition(ctx, *value),
272	
273	            Event::Focus { is_keyboard } => {
274	                let is_keyboard = *is_keyboard;
275	                if ctx.focused && ctx.focus_visible == is_keyboard {
276	                    return None;
277	                }
278	
279	                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {
280	                    ctx.focused = true;
281	                    ctx.focus_visible = is_keyboard;
282	                }))
283	            }
284	
285	            Event::Blur => {
286	                if !ctx.focused && !ctx.focus_visible {
287	                    return None;
288	                }
289	
290	                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(|ctx: &mut Context| {
291	                    ctx.focused = false;
292	                    ctx.focus_visible = false;
293	                }))
294	            }
295	
296	            Event::SyncProps => Some(sync_props_plan(ctx, props)),
297	
298	            Event::SyncControlledOpen(value) => {
299	                let value = *value;
300	                let next = state_from_bool(value);
301	
302	                let mut next_open = ctx.open.clone();
303	                next_open.set(value);
304	                next_open.sync_controlled(Some(value));
305	
306	                if ctx.open == next_open && state == &next {
307	                    return None;
308	                }
309	
310	                Some(TransitionPlan::to(next).apply(move |ctx: &mut Context| {
311	                    ctx.open.set(value);
312	                    ctx.open.sync_controlled(Some(value));
313	                }))
314	            }
315	
316	            _ => None,
317	        }
318	    }
319	
320	    fn connect<'a>(
321	        state: &'a Self::State,
322	        ctx: &'a Self::Context,
323	        props: &'a Self::Props,
324	        send: &'a dyn Fn(Self::Event),
325	    ) -> Self::Api<'a> {
326	        Api {
327	            state,
328	            ctx,
329	            props,
330	            send,
331	        }
332	    }
333	
334	    fn on_props_changed(old: &Self::Props, new: &Self::Props) -> Vec<Self::Event> {
335	        assert_eq!(
336	            old.id, new.id,
337	            "collapsible::Props.id must remain stable after init"
338	        );
339	
340	        let mut events = Vec::new();
341	
342	        let prop_backed_context_changed = old.disabled != new.disabled
343	            || old.collapsed_height != new.collapsed_height
344	            || old.collapsed_width != new.collapsed_width
345	            || (old.open.is_some() && new.open.is_none());
346	
347	        if prop_backed_context_changed {
348	            events.push(Event::SyncProps);
349	        }
350	
351	        if old.open != new.open
352	            && let Some(open) = new.open
353	        {
354	            events.push(Event::SyncControlledOpen(open));
355	        }
356	
357	        events
358	    }
359	}

361	/// Structural parts exposed by the `Collapsible` connect API.

364	pub enum Part {
365	    /// The root collapsible container.
366	    Root,
367	
368	    /// The button that toggles the content region.
369	    Trigger,
370	
371	    /// Optional visual indicator for the current open state.
372	    Indicator,
373	
374	    /// The expandable content region.

378	/// Connected Collapsible API.
379	pub struct Api<'a> {
380	    state: &'a State,
381	    ctx: &'a Context,
382	    props: &'a Props,

384	}
385	
386	impl Debug for Api<'_> {

388	        f.debug_struct("Api")
389	            .field("state", self.state)
390	            .field("ctx", self.ctx)
391	            .field("props", self.props)
392	            .finish()
393	    }
394	}

396	impl Api<'_> {
397	    /// Whether the collapsible is currently open.
398	    #[must_use]

400	        self.state == &State::Open
401	    }

403	    /// Attributes for the root container element.
404	    #[must_use]
405	    pub fn root_attrs(&self) -> AttrMap {
406	        let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();
407	        let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = Part::Root.data_attrs();
408	
409	        attrs
410	            .set(scope_attr, scope_val)
411	            .set(part_attr, part_val)
412	            .set(HtmlAttr::Id, self.ctx.ids.id())
413	            .set(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-state"), state_token(self.is_open()));
414	
415	        if self.ctx.disabled {
416	            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-disabled"), true);
417	        }
418	
419	        attrs
420	    }
421	
422	    /// Attributes for the trigger button.
423	    #[must_use]
424	    pub fn trigger_attrs(&self) -> AttrMap {
425	        let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();
426	        let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = Part::Trigger.data_attrs();
427	
428	        let label = if self.is_open() {
429	            (self.ctx.messages.collapse_label)(&self.ctx.locale)
430	        } else {
431	            (self.ctx.messages.expand_label)(&self.ctx.locale)
432	        };
433	
434	        attrs
435	            .set(HtmlAttr::Id, self.trigger_id())
436	            .set(scope_attr, scope_val)
437	            .set(part_attr, part_val)
438	            .set(HtmlAttr::Type, "button")
439	            .set(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-state"), state_token(self.is_open()))
440	            .set(
441	                HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Expanded),
442	                bool_token(self.is_open()),
443	            )
444	            .set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Controls), self.content_id())
445	            .set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Label), label);
446	
447	        if self.ctx.disabled {
448	            attrs
449	                .set_bool(HtmlAttr::Disabled, true)
450	                .set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-disabled"), true);
451	        }
452	
453	        if self.ctx.focused {
454	            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-focus"), true);
455	        }
456	
457	        if self.ctx.focus_visible {
458	            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-focus-visible"), true);
459	        }
460	
461	        attrs
462	    }
463	
464	    /// Attributes for an optional visual indicator.
465	    #[must_use]
466	    pub fn indicator_attrs(&self) -> AttrMap {
467	        let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();
468	        let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = Part::Indicator.data_attrs();
469	
470	        attrs
471	            .set(scope_attr, scope_val)
472	            .set(part_attr, part_val)
473	            .set(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-state"), state_token(self.is_open()))
474	            .set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Hidden), "true");
475	
476	        attrs
477	    }
478	
479	    /// Attributes for the content region.
480	    #[must_use]
481	    pub fn content_attrs(&self) -> AttrMap {
482	        let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();
483	        let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = Part::Content.data_attrs();
484	
485	        let has_collapsed_size =
486	            self.ctx.collapsed_height.is_some() || self.ctx.collapsed_width.is_some();
487	
488	        attrs
489	            .set(HtmlAttr::Id, self.content_id())
490	            .set(scope_attr, scope_val)
491	            .set(part_attr, part_val)
492	            .set(HtmlAttr::Role, "region")
493	            .set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::LabelledBy), self.trigger_id())
494	            .set(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-state"), state_token(self.is_open()));
495	
496	        if !self.is_open() && !has_collapsed_size {
497	            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Hidden, true);
498	        }
499	
500	        if let Some(height) = &self.ctx.collapsed_height {
501	            attrs.set_style(
502	                CssProperty::Custom("ars-collapsible-collapsed-height"),
503	                height,
504	            );
505	        }
506	
507	        if let Some(width) = &self.ctx.collapsed_width {
508	            attrs.set_style(
509	                CssProperty::Custom("ars-collapsible-collapsed-width"),
510	                width,
511	            );
512	        }
513	
514	        if has_collapsed_size {
515	            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data("ars-collapsed-size"), true);
516	        }
517	
518	        attrs
519	    }

521	    /// Adapter handler: the trigger was clicked.
522	    pub fn on_trigger_click(&self) {
523	        if !self.ctx.disabled {
524	            (self.send)(Event::Toggle);

528	    /// Adapter handler: a key was pressed on the trigger.
529	    ///
530	    /// Returns `true` when the key was handled so adapters can prevent the
531	    /// native button activation click and avoid dispatching a duplicate toggle.
532	    pub fn on_trigger_keydown(&self, data: &KeyboardEventData) -> bool {
533	        if !self.ctx.disabled
534	            && !data.repeat
535	            && (data.key == KeyboardKey::Enter || data.key == KeyboardKey::Space)
536	        {
537	            (self.send)(Event::Toggle);
538	            return true;
539	        }
540	
541	        false
542	    }
543	
544	    /// Adapter handler: the trigger received focus.
545	    pub fn on_trigger_focus(&self, is_keyboard: bool) {
546	        if !self.ctx.disabled {
547	            (self.send)(Event::Focus { is_keyboard });
548	        }
549	    }

565	impl ConnectApi for Api<'_> {
566	    type Part = Part;
567	
568	    fn part_attrs(&self, part: Self::Part) -> AttrMap {
569	        match part {
570	            Part::Root => self.root_attrs(),
571	            Part::Trigger => self.trigger_attrs(),
572	            Part::Indicator => self.indicator_attrs(),
573	            Part::Content => self.content_attrs(),
574	        }

577	
578	fn open_transition(ctx: &Context, value: bool) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Machine>> {
579	    if ctx.open.is_controlled() {
580	        return Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {
581	            ctx.open.set(value);
582	        }));
583	    }
584	
585	    if ctx.open.get() == &value {
586	        return None;
587	    }
588	
589	    Some(
590	        TransitionPlan::to(state_from_bool(value)).apply(move |ctx: &mut Context| {
591	            ctx.open.set(value);
592	        }),
593	    )
594	}
595	
596	fn sync_props_plan(ctx: &Context, props: &Props) -> TransitionPlan<Machine> {
597	    let disabled = props.disabled;
598	    let collapsed_height = props.collapsed_height.clone();
599	    let collapsed_width = props.collapsed_width.clone();
600	    let was_controlled = ctx.open.is_controlled();
601	    let leaving_controlled = was_controlled && props.open.is_none();
602	    let visible_open = *ctx.open.get();
603	
604	    let target_state = if leaving_controlled {
605	        Some(state_from_bool(visible_open))
606	    } else {
607	        None
608	    };
609	
610	    let mut plan = if let Some(state) = target_state {
611	        TransitionPlan::to(state)
612	    } else {
613	        TransitionPlan::new()
614	    };
615	
616	    plan = plan.apply(move |ctx: &mut Context| {
617	        ctx.disabled = disabled;
618	        ctx.collapsed_height = collapsed_height;
619	        ctx.collapsed_width = collapsed_width;
620	
621	        if leaving_controlled {
622	            ctx.open.set(visible_open);
623	            ctx.open.sync_controlled(None);
624	        }
625	
626	        if ctx.disabled {
627	            ctx.focused = false;
628	            ctx.focus_visible = false;
629	        }
630	    });
631	
632	    plan
633	}
634	
635	const fn state_from_bool(open: bool) -> State {
636	    if open { State::Open } else { State::Closed }
637	}
638	
639	const fn bool_token(value: bool) -> &'static str {
640	    if value { "true" } else { "false" }
641	}
642	
643	const fn state_token(open: bool) -> &'static str {
644	    if open { "open" } else { "closed" }
645	}

/// Typed side-effect intents emitted by the `RatingGroup` machine.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum Effect {
    /// Notify adapters that the user requested a new committed value.
    ValueChange,
}

/// Structural parts exposed by the `RatingGroup` connect API.
#[derive(ComponentPart)]
#[scope = "rating-group"]
pub enum Part {
    /// The root rating group element.
    Root,

    /// The visible label element.
    Label,

    /// The interactive rating control.
    Control,

    /// One rating item slot.
    Item {
        /// Zero-based item index.
        index: usize,
    },

    /// Hidden input used for native form submission.
    HiddenInput,
}

/// Machine for the `RatingGroup` component.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Machine;

impl ars_core::Machine for Machine {

impl ConnectApi for Api<'_> {
    type Part = Part;

    fn part_attrs(&self, part: Self::Part) -> AttrMap {
        match part {
            Part::Root => self.root_attrs(),
            Part::Viewport => self.viewport_attrs(),
            Part::Content => self.content_attrs(),
            Part::ScrollbarY => self.scrollbar_y_attrs(),
            Part::ThumbY => self.thumb_y_attrs(),
            Part::ScrollbarX => self.scrollbar_x_attrs(),
            Part::ThumbX => self.thumb_x_attrs(),
            Part::CornerSquare => self.corner_square_attrs(),
        }
    }
}

        }),
        (0usize..4).prop_map(|handle_index| splitter::Event::HandleFocus { handle_index }),
        Just(splitter::Event::HandleBlur),
        (0usize..4).prop_map(|panel_index| splitter::Event::CollapsePanel { panel_index }),
        (0usize..4).prop_map(|panel_index| splitter::Event::ExpandPanel { panel_index }),
        prop::collection::vec(0.0f64..100.0, 0..5)
            .prop_map(|sizes| splitter::Event::SetSizes { sizes }),
    ]

fn arb_splitter_step() -> impl Strategy<Value = SplitterStep> {
    prop_oneof![
        arb_splitter_event().prop_map(SplitterStep::Send),
        arb_splitter_props().prop_map(SplitterStep::SetProps),
    ]
}

fn assert_splitter_invariants(service: &Service<splitter::Machine>) -> TestCaseResult {
    let sizes = service.context().sizes.get();

    prop_assert_eq!(sizes.len(), service.context().panels.len());
    prop_assert!(sizes.iter().all(|size| size.is_finite()));
    prop_assert!(service.context().keyboard_step.is_finite());
    prop_assert!(service.context().drag_scale_factor.is_finite());

    if let Some(handle_index) = service.context().focused_handle {
        prop_assert!(handle_index + 1 < sizes.len());
    }

    if let splitter::State::Dragging { handle_index } = service.state() {
        prop_assert!(*handle_index + 1 < sizes.len());
        prop_assert_eq!(service.context().drag_start_sizes.len(), sizes.len());
    }

    Ok(())
}

proptest! {
    #![proptest_config(super::common::proptest_config())]

    #[test]
    #[ignore = "proptest — nightly extended-proptest job"]
    fn proptest_splitter_event_sequences_preserve_invariants(
        props in arb_splitter_props(),
        steps in prop::collection::vec(arb_splitter_step(), 0..128),
    ) {
        let mut service = Service::<splitter::Machine>::new(
            props,
            &Env::default(),
            &splitter::Messages::default(),
        );

        assert_splitter_invariants(&service)?;

        for step in steps {
            match step {
                SplitterStep::Send(event) => {
                    drop(service.send(event));
                }

                SplitterStep::SetProps(props) => {
                    drop(service.set_props(props));
                }
            }

            assert_splitter_invariants(&service)?;
        }
    }
}

> AGENT

My `Always`-mode visibility invariant is too strong — `HideTimeout` hides scrollbars in any mode (per spec it's unconditional; adapters only emit it in `Scroll` mode). Remove that invariant.

> TOOL

Instead, a `Scroll` event in\n`ScrollbarVisibility::Scroll` mode transitions to `State::ScrollActive` and emits\nthe named `Effect::AutoHide` intent. The adapter is responsible for:\n\n1. Sending `Event::HideTimeout` back to the machine when the timer fires.\n\nThe machine's `HideTimeout` handler then hides the scrollbars and returns to\n`State::Idle` (unless a thumb drag is in progress). Because each new `Scroll`\nevent re-emits `Effect::AutoHide`, the adapter should treat a fresh intent as a\n\"reset the timer\" signal, keeping the scrollbar visible while scrolling\ncontinues.\n\n### 1.7 Connect / API"

Activates the spec'd-but-dead field + makes it testable | spec §1.3/1.4/1.6 + impl + test |
| L1 | Low | `State` derives `Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Default` | impl also derives `Copy` | `Copy` (trivial fieldless enum; all sibling layout machines derive it) — add to spec | spec §1.1 |
| L2 | Low | `normalize_scroll_left` doc lists 3 RTL conventions (incl. Legacy Firefox) | impl doc dropped the Legacy Firefox line | Restore the 3rd convention in the impl doc for parity | impl |

Items checked and confirmed **not** drift: `Axis`/`Effect`/`type Effect`/auto-hide (already aligned), all 8 `Part`s, every `Api` method signature, `Event`/`Context`/`ScrollOrientation`/`ScrollbarVisibility` derives, `ScrollDetail` (pub data type for adapters), and `orientation` being unused by core visibility (deliberate — it's an adapter render/CSS concern, the adapter chooses which scrollbar parts to render).

Disposition: 2 spec+impl changes, 1 spec-only (Copy), 1 impl-only (doc). Landing M1 now.

  "old_string": "    #[test]\n    fn both_axes_track_shortened_by_cross_scrollbar_gap() {\n        // With both scrollbars visible, axis_metrics subtracts the cross-axis\n        // thickness from the track. cross_size defaults to 0, so the click\n        // math is unaffected, but this exercises the both-visible branch.\n        let mut service = service(props().scrollbar_visibility(ScrollbarVisibility::Always));\n        resize(&mut service, 100.0, 100.0, 400.0, 400.0);\n        assert!(service.context().scrollbar_x_visible);\n        assert!(service.context().scrollbar_y_visible);\n\n        drop(service.send(Event::Scroll { x: 0.0, y: 150.0 }));\n        drop(service.send(Event::TrackClick {\n            pos: 10.0,\n            axis: Axis::Y,\n        }));\n        assert_eq!(service.context().scroll_y, 50.0);\n    }",
  "new_string": "    #[test]\n    fn both_axes_track_shortened_by_cross_scrollbar_gap() {\n        // With both scrollbars visible, axis_metrics subtracts the cross-axis\n        // thickness from each track so the thumb does not overlap the corner.\n        let mut service = service(\n            props()\n                .scrollbar_visibility(ScrollbarVisibility::Always)\n                .scrollbar_cross_size(8.0),\n        );\n        resize(&mut service, 100.0, 100.0, 400.0, 400.0);\n        assert!(service.context().scrollbar_x_visible);\n        assert!(service.context().scrollbar_y_visible);\n        drop(service.send(Event::Scroll { x: 0.0, y: 150.0 }));\n\n        // Track shortened to 100 - 8 = 92. thumb_size = (100/400)*92 = 23,\n        // thumb_pos = (150/300)*(92-23) = 34.5 (vs 37.5 with a full track).\n        drop(service.send(Event::ThumbDragStart {\n            pos: 0.0,\n            axis: Axis::Y,\n        }));\n        assert_close(service.context().drag_start_thumb_pos, 34.5);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn cross_size_defaults_to_zero_when_unset() {\n        // Without the prop, the cross-axis gap is 0, so the track keeps its\n        // full length and the thumb position is unshortened.\n        let mut service = service(props().scrollbar_visibility(ScrollbarVisibility::Always));\n        resize(&mut service, 100.0, 100.0, 400.0, 400.0);\n        drop(service.send(Event::Scroll { x: 0.0, y: 150.0 }));\n\n        drop(service.send(Event::ThumbDragStart {\n            pos: 0.0,\n            axis: Axis::Y,\n        }));\n        assert_close(service.context().drag_start_thumb_pos, 37.5);\n    }"
}

> AGENT

Implementation and the full post-implementation audit are complete. Here is the consolidated result for your review.

## Task #279 — ScrollArea agnostic core

**New module:** [scroll_area/mod.rs](crates/ars-components/src/layout/scroll_area/mod.rs) — `State` (Idle/Hovering/ScrollActive/ThumbDragging), `Event`, `Axis`, `Context`, `Props`, `Messages`, `Effect`, `Machine`, 8-part `Part` enum, `Api` + `ConnectApi`, and the pure helpers `compute_thumb_metrics` / `thumb_pos_to_scroll` / `normalize_scroll_left`. Wired into [layout/mod.rs](crates/ars-components/src/layout/mod.rs).

**Key design decision (drift fixed in both spec + code):** the spec example embedded a platform `set_timeout` auto-hide timer *inside* the agnostic machine. Timers are an adapter concern, so I converted it to the workspace's named-intent pattern (`Effect::AutoHide`, mirroring `tooltip`): the core emits the intent and the adapter owns the timer + sends `Event::HideTimeout` back. I also defined the previously-undefined `Axis` enum. The Leptos `leptos` skill / Dioxus specs already described adapter-owned timer ownership, so they were consistent.

### Audit findings (all landed in this PR)

**Phase 1 — spec/impl drift**
| | Finding | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | `Context.scrollbar_cross_size` was used by `axis_metrics` but no event/prop ever set it (dead field) | Added `Props::scrollbar_cross_size` (mirrors `min_thumb_size`), read at `init` — in spec §1.3/1.4/1.6 + impl + 2 tests |
| L1 | `State` derived `Copy` in impl but not spec | Added `Copy` to spec (conventional for fieldless enums) |
| L2 | impl doc dropped the Legacy-Firefox RTL convention | Restored for parity |

**Phase 2 (2 clean rounds):** added `scrollbar_cross_size` to both adapter-spec prop sketches for the "full props parity" claim. Confirmed manifest/catalog already registered, no adapter feature wiring needed (adapter components out of scope), and the `Api` read surface matches the spec exactly (so I did *not* invent extra getters).

**Phase 3 — coverage:** **97.48% line / 98.39% region** on the module. The 3 uncovered lines are all justified: `compute_thumb_metrics`'s `else 0.0` (unreachable after the early `content ≤ viewport` return), and the `AutoHide` setup-closure body (adapter-invoked, same as `rating_group`). Added tests for the MouseEnter-outside-Hover branch, the `Axis::X` track-click + cross-size branch, and the `Api` Debug impl.

### Tests (all named acceptance tests pass)
43 inline unit/snapshot tests, 13 committed `.snap` fixtures, 1 spec-conformance anatomy test, 1 proptest (nightly-ignored). Full suite: **4109 passed, 0 failed**. Clippy `-D warnings` clean, doc clean, no snapshot orphans, spec validate + compile-snippets green.

### ⚠️ One out-of-scope change to flag
`crates/ars-components/src/navigation/pagination/mod.rs` (1 line): `map_or_else(.., identity)` → `unwrap_or_else(..)`. This is a **pre-existing** `clippy::unnecessary_option_map_or_else` error (committed at HEAD, untouched by me) that the current floating `@stable` toolchain (1.96.0, released 4 days ago) now denies. Because it's in the same crate, it blocks *any* clippy run on `ars-components` — including this PR's CI gate. It's a zero-risk mechanical fix. **If you'd prefer I drop it and handle it separately, say so and I'll revert it.**

Next steps after your approval: run `cargo xci-fast`, then commit + open a PR to `main` (`Closes #279`, `snapshot-reviewed` label), then the Codex review loop. **I have not committed anything.** Want me to proceed?

> AGENT

Both conventions exist, but **delay-with-a-default** fields (tooltip `open_delay`/`close_delay`, hover_card, avatar `fallback_delay`) use plain `Duration` with a `Default` value — `Option<Duration>` is reserved for "None means off/no-dismiss". Since `hide_delay` always has a value, plain `Duration` is the right match. I'll rename `hide_delay_ms` → `hide_delay` (dropping the now-wrong unit suffix, like `open_delay`) and switch the type to `Duration`.

> AGENT

Codex finished with **6 unresolved P2 threads** (no 👍). I've analyzed each against the code and spec. Five are clear correctness bugs I should fix; one reverses a design decision I made during the audit, so I want your call on it before implementing.

**Clear bugs (I agree — will fix with TDD + spec sync):**

1. **Clamp thumb drag** (line 774) — `new_thumb_pos` is clamped at 0 but not at the top, so dragging past the track end produces a scroll offset beyond `content − viewport` (e.g. 800 when max is 300). Real bug in both spec and impl. Fix: clamp to `[0, track_size − thumb_size]`.
2. **Resize doesn't clear stale visibility** (line 631) — `update_visibility()` no-ops for Hover/Scroll, so if a resize removes overflow, the scrollbar stays `data-ars-visible="true"`. Fix: clear flags for non-overflowing axes in all modes.
3. **Scroll-mode drag-end never restarts the hide timer** (line 786) — `ThumbDragEnd` returns to Idle without re-emitting `Effect::AutoHide`, so in `Scroll` mode the scrollbar can stay visible forever after a drag. Fix: re-emit `AutoHide` on drag-end in Scroll mode.
4. **Hover stuck visible after leaving an overlaid track** (line 692) — sequence root-enter → scrollbar-enter → root-leave → scrollbar-leave leaves it in `Hovering`, because `MouseLeaveScrollbar` only clears the flag and never hides. Fix: track root-hover separately so the last leave (root or scrollbar) hides.
5. **`on_props_changed` not implemented** (line 563) — controlled prop changes (`scrollbar_visibility`, `min_thumb_size`, `hide_delay`, `scrollbar_cross_size`, `dir`) never sync into `Context` on rerender; stale until remount. Fix: add a `SyncProps` event + `on_props_changed`, like `collapsible`.

**The judgment call (Thread 1, line 255 — gate visibility by orientation):**
Codex says a `Vertical` ScrollArea should never set `scrollbar_x_visible = true`, even with horizontal overflow. During the audit I deliberately left orientation *out* of the core visibility math, reasoning it's an adapter render/CSS concern (the adapter renders only the parts its orientation allows, and sets `overflow-x: hidden` so no x-overflow is reported). Codex's counter is that the visibility flags are authoritative and a naive adapter would expose an unwanted scrollbar.

On reflection I now lean toward **Codex being right** — gating in the core makes the flags self-consistent and removes an adapter footgun. But it reverses my documented audit decision and adds `orientation` to `Context` + the spec contract, so I want your call.

  "new_string": "    /// Whether the horizontal scrollbar is permitted to be visible: the\n    /// orientation must enable it and (outside `Always` mode) the content must\n    /// overflow.\n    #[must_use]\n    fn can_show_x(&self) -> bool {\n        self.orientation.allows_x()\n            && (self.scrollbar_visibility == ScrollbarVisibility::Always || self.has_overflow_x())\n    }\n\n    /// Whether the vertical scrollbar is permitted to be visible.\n    #[must_use]\n    fn can_show_y(&self) -> bool {\n        self.orientation.allows_y()\n            && (self.scrollbar_visibility == ScrollbarVisibility::Always || self.has_overflow_y())\n    }\n\n    /// Recompute scrollbar visibility after a metrics or prop change.\n    ///\n    /// `Always` and `Auto` derive visibility directly from orientation and\n    /// overflow. `Hover` and `Scroll` are event-driven, but this still clamps\n    /// their flags off for any axis the orientation disables or that no longer\n    /// overflows, so a stale scrollbar cannot linger after a resize.\n    pub fn update_visibility(&mut self) {\n        match self.scrollbar_visibility {\n            ScrollbarVisibility::Always | ScrollbarVisibility::Auto => {\n                self.scrollbar_x_visible = self.can_show_x();\n                self.scrollbar_y_visible = self.can_show_y();\n            }\n\n            ScrollbarVisibility::Hover | ScrollbarVisibility::Scroll => {\n                self.scrollbar_x_visible &= self.can_show_x();\n                self.scrollbar_y_visible &= self.can_show_y();\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}"
}

result = service.send(Event::MouseEnter);\n\n        assert!(!result.state_changed);\n        assert_eq!(service.state(), &State::Idle);\n        assert!(service.context().hovering_root);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn hover_scrollbar_outliving_root_hides_on_scrollbar_leave() {\n        // root enter -> scrollbar enter -> root leave -> scrollbar leave: the\n        // final scrollbar leave must hide, since no further root-leave arrives.\n        let mut service = service(\n            props()\n                .orientation(ScrollOrientation::Both)\n                .scrollbar_visibility(ScrollbarVisibility::Hover),\n        );\n        resize(&mut service, 100.0, 100.0, 400.0, 400.0);\n\n        drop(service.send(Event::MouseEnter));\n assert!(service.context().scrollbar_y_visible);\n\n        let result = service.send(Event::MouseLeaveScrollbar);\n\n        assert!(result.state_changed);\n        assert_eq!(service.state(), &State::Idle);\n        assert!(!service.context().scrollbar_x_visible);\n        assert!(!service.context().scrollbar_y_visible);\n    }\n\n    // --- orientation gating assert!(both.context().scrollbar_x_visible);\n        assert!(both.context().scrollbar_y_visible);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn always_mode_is_gated_by_orientation() {\n        // `Always` shows  .scrollbar_visibility(ScrollbarVisibility::Always),\n        );\n        assert!(service.context().scrollbar_y_visible);\n        assert!(!service.context().scrollbar_x_visible);\n    }\n\n    // --- assert!(service.context().scrollbar_y_visible);\n\n        // Content shrinks so the axis no longer overflows; the previously-shown\n        // scrollbar must clear even though Scroll mode is
