viewport 100 = 300), not overshoot to 800.\n        drop(service.send(Event::ThumbDragMove { pos: 200.0 }));\n        assert_eq!(service.context().scroll_y, 300.0);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn scroll_mode_drag_end_restarts_auto_hide() {\n        let mut service = service(props().scrollbar_visibility(ScrollbarVisibility::Scroll));\n        resize(&mut service, 100.0, 100.0, 100.0, 400.0);\n        drop(service.send(Event::Scroll { x: 0.0, y: 150.0 }));\n        drop(service.send(Event::ThumbDragStart {\n            pos: 0.0,\n            axis: Axis::Y,\n        }));\n\n        let result = service.send(Event::ThumbDragEnd);\n\n        // Drag-end in Scroll mode must restart the adapter-owned hide timer so\n        // the scrollbar fades instead of lingering.\n        assert_eq!(service.state(), &State::ScrollActive);\n        assert_eq!(service.context().drag_axis, None);\n        assert!(\n            result\n                .pending_effects\n                .iter()\n                .any(|effect| effect.name == Effect::AutoHide),\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn drag_end_outside_scroll_mode_returns_to_idle() {\n        let mut service = service(props());\n        resize(&mut service, 100.0, 100.0, 100.0, 400.0);\n        drop(service.send(Event::ThumbDragStart {\n            pos: 0.0,\n            axis: Axis::Y,\n        }));\n\n        let result = service.send(Event::ThumbDragEnd);\n\n        assert_eq!(service.state(), &State::Idle);\n        assert_eq!(service.context().drag_axis, None);\n        assert!(result.pending_effects.is_empty());\n    }\n\n    // --- track click --------------------------------------------------------"

287	/// Inverse: given a thumb position, compute the scroll position.
288	pub fn thumb_pos_to_scroll(
289	    thumb_pos: f64,
290	    track_size: f64,
291	    thumb_size: f64,
292	    content_size: f64,
293	    viewport_size: f64,
294	) -> f64 {
295	    let scrollable_track = track_size - thumb_size;
296	    let scrollable_content = content_size - viewport_size;
297	    if scrollable_track <= 0.0 { return 0.0; }
298	    (thumb_pos / scrollable_track) * scrollable_content
299	}

302	### 1.6 Full Machine Implementation
303	
304	```rust
305	/// Typed side-effect intents emitted by the `ScrollArea` machine.
306	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
307	pub enum Effect {
308	    /// Start (or restart) the auto-hide timer in `Scroll` visibility mode.
309	    ///
310	    /// The adapter owns the timer: it waits `Context::hide_delay` and then
311	    /// sends `Event::HideTimeout` back to the machine. The agnostic core
312	    /// never schedules timers itself.
313	    AutoHide,
314	}
315	
316	pub struct Machine;
317	
318	impl ars_core::Machine for Machine {
319	    type State = State;
320	    type Event = Event;
321	    type Context = Context;
322	    type Props = Props;
323	    type Messages = Messages;
324	    type Effect = Effect;
325	    type Api<'a> = Api<'a>;
326	
327	    fn init(props: &Self::Props, env: &Env, messages: &Self::Messages) -> (Self::State, Self::Context) {
328	        let locale = env.locale.clone();
329	        let messages = messages.clone();
330	        let mut ctx = Context {
331	            scroll_x: 0.0, scroll_y: 0.0,
332	            viewport_width: 0.0, viewport_height: 0.0,
333	            content_width: 0.0, content_height: 0.0,
334	            scrollbar_x_visible: false, scrollbar_y_visible: false,
335	            hovering_scrollbar: false,
336	            scrollbar_visibility: props.scrollbar_visibility,
337	            min_thumb_size: props.min_thumb_size.unwrap_or(20.0),
338	            hide_delay: props.hide_delay,
339	            scrollbar_cross_size: props.scrollbar_cross_size.unwrap_or(0.0),
340	            drag_start_pointer_pos: 0.0,
341	            drag_start_thumb_pos: 0.0,
342	            drag_start_scroll_pos: 0.0,
343	            drag_axis: None,
344	            ids: ComponentIds::from_id(&props.id),
345	            dir: props.dir.unwrap_or(Direction::Ltr),
346	            locale,
347	            messages,
348	        };
349	        ctx.update_visibility();
350	        (State::Idle, ctx)
351	    }
352	
353	    fn transition(
354	        state: &Self::State,
355	        event: &Self::Event,
356	        ctx: &Self::Context,
357	        props: &Self::Props,
358	    ) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Self>> {
359	        match event {
360	            Event::Resize { viewport_width, viewport_height, content_width, content_height } => {
361	                let (vw, vh, cw, ch) = (*viewport_width, *viewport_height, *content_width, *content_height);
362	                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| {
363	                    ctx.viewport_width = vw; ctx.viewport_height = vh;
364	                    ctx.content_width = cw; ctx.content_height = ch;
365	                    ctx.update_visibility();
366	                }))
367	            }
368	
369	            Event::Scroll { x, y } => {
370	                let (sx, sy) = (*x, *y);
371	                if ctx.scrollbar_visibility == ScrollbarVisibility::Scroll {
372	                    // The agnostic core does not own timers. It records the
373	                    // `Effect::AutoHide` intent; the adapter starts a
374	                    // `ctx.hide_delay` timer and sends `Event::HideTimeout`
375	                    // back when it fires. See §1.6.1.
376	                    Some(TransitionPlan::to(State::ScrollActive).apply(move |ctx| {
377	                        ctx.scroll_x = sx; ctx.scroll_y = sy;
378	                        ctx.scrollbar_x_visible = ctx.has_overflow_x();
379	                        ctx.scrollbar_y_visible = ctx.has_overflow_y();
380	                    }).with_named_effect(Effect::AutoHide, |_ctx, _props, _send| no_cleanup()))
381	                } else {
382	                    Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| {
383	                        ctx.scroll_x = sx; ctx.scroll_y = sy;
384	                    }))
385	                }
386	            }
387	
388	            Event::MouseEnter => {
389	                if ctx.scrollbar_visibility == ScrollbarVisibility::Hover {
390	                    Some(TransitionPlan::to(State::Hovering).apply(|ctx| {
391	                        ctx.scrollbar_x_visible = ctx.has_overflow_x();
392	                        ctx.scrollbar_y_visible = ctx.has_overflow_y();
393	                    }))
394	                } else { None }
395	            }
396	
397	            Event::MouseLeave => {
398	                if ctx.scrollbar_visibility == ScrollbarVisibility::Hover && !ctx.hovering_scrollbar {
399	                    Some(TransitionPlan::to(State::Idle).apply(|ctx| {
400	                        ctx.scrollbar_x_visible = false; ctx.scrollbar_y_visible = false;
401	                    }))
402	                } else { None }
403	            }
404	
405	            Event::MouseEnterScrollbar => Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(|ctx| { ctx.hovering_scrollbar = true; })),
406	            Event::MouseLeaveScrollbar => Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(|ctx| { ctx.hovering_scrollbar = false; })),
407	
408	            Event::HideTimeout => {
409	                if *state != State::ThumbDragging {

411	                        ctx.scrollbar_x_visible = false; ctx.scrollbar_y_visible = false;
412	                    }))
413	                } else { None }
414	            }

417	                let (p, a) = (*pos, *axis);
418	                let scroll_pos = match a { Axis::X => ctx.scroll_x, Axis::Y => ctx.scroll_y };
419	                let (viewport_size, content_size, track_size) = axis_metrics(ctx, a);
420	                let min_thumb = ctx.min_thumb_size;
421	                Some(TransitionPlan::to(State::ThumbDragging).apply(move |ctx| {

423	                    let (_, current_thumb_pos) = compute_thumb_metrics(

425	                    );
426	                    ctx.drag_start_thumb_pos = current_thumb_pos;
427	                    ctx.drag_start_scroll_pos = scroll_pos;
428	                    ctx.drag_axis = Some(a);
429	                }))

432	            Event::ThumbDragMove { pos } => {
433	                if *state != State::ThumbDragging { return None; }
434	                let axis = ctx.drag_axis?;
435	                let p = *pos;
436	                let (drag_start_pointer, drag_start_thumb, drag_scroll, min_thumb) =
437	                    (ctx.drag_start_pointer_pos, ctx.drag_start_thumb_pos, ctx.drag_start_scroll_pos, ctx.min_thumb_size);
438	                let (viewport_size, content_size, track_size) = axis_metrics(ctx, axis);
439	                let delta = p - drag_start_pointer;
440	                let (thumb_size, _) = compute_thumb_metrics(viewport_size, content_size, drag_scroll, track_size, min_thumb);
441	                let new_thumb_pos = (drag_start_thumb + delta).max(0.0);
442	                let new_scroll = thumb_pos_to_scroll(new_thumb_pos, track_size, thumb_size, content_size, viewport_size);
443	                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| {
444	                    match axis { Axis::X => ctx.scroll_x = new_scroll, Axis::Y => ctx.scroll_y = new_scroll }
445	                }))
446	            }
447	
448	            Event::ThumbDragEnd => {
449	                Some(TransitionPlan::to(State::Idle).apply(|ctx| { ctx.drag_axis = None; }))
450	            }

453	                let (a, p) = (*axis, *pos);
454	                let scroll_pos = match a { Axis::X => ctx.scroll_x, Axis::Y => ctx.scroll_y };

Emitted by `on_props_changed`.\n            Event::SyncProps => {\n                let orientation = props.orientation;\n                let visibility = props.scrollbar_visibility;\n                let min_thumb = props.min_thumb_size.unwrap_or(20.0);\n                let hide_delay = props.hide_delay;\n                let cross = props.scrollbar_cross_size.unwrap_or(0.0);\n                let dir = props.dir.unwrap_or(Direction::Ltr);\n                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| {\n                    ctx.orientation = orientation;\n                    ctx.scrollbar_visibility = visibility;\n                    ctx.min_thumb_size = min_thumb;\n                    ctx.hide_delay = hide_delay;\n                    ctx.scrollbar_cross_size = cross;\n                    ctx.dir = dir;\n                    ctx.update_visibility();\n                }))\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn connect<'a>(\n        state: &'a State, ctx: &'a Context, props: &'a Props, send: &'a dyn Fn(Event),\n    ) -> Api<'a> {\n        Api { state, ctx, props, send }\n    }\n\n    /// Sync prop-backed context fields when a controlled prop changes so adapter\n    /// rerenders are not ignored until remount. `id`, `locale`, and `aria_label`\n    /// are read live and need no sync.\n    fn on_props_changed(old: &Self::Props, new: &Self::Props) -> Vec<Self::Event> {\n        let changed = old.orientation != new.orientation\n            || old.scrollbar_visibility != new.scrollbar_visibility\n            || old.min_thumb_size != new.min_thumb_size\n            || old.hide_delay != new.hide_delay\n            || old.scrollbar_cross_size != new.scrollbar_cross_size\n            || old.dir != new.dir;\n        if changed { vec![Event::SyncProps] } else { Vec::new() }\n    }\n}"

THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F6F10
  db=3329545299 crates/ars-components/src/layout/scroll_area/mod.rs:912
  **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Cancel stale auto-hide timer when visibility mode changes**

When a scrolled `ScrollArea` is in `ScrollbarVisibility::Scroll`, an `AutoHide` effect is active; if props then change to `Always`/`Auto`, this `SyncProps` transition only mutates context and never cancels the named effect or leaves `ScrollActive`. I checked the Leptos/Dioxus `use_machine` effect handling, and active cleanups are only removed on a state change, explicit `cancel_effects`, or replacement pending effect, so the old timer can still send `HideTimeout` after the component is now `Always` and hide both scrollbars. Add an explicit `Effect::AutoHide` cancellation or state transition when syncing away from `Scroll` mode.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F6F12
  db=3329545301 crates/ars-components/src/layout/scroll_area/mod.rs:580
  **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clamp track length after subtracting the corner gap**

When both scrollbars are visible and `scrollbar_cross_size` is larger than the current viewport extent on an axis, this subtraction returns a negative `track_size`. That value is fed into `compute_thumb_metrics`, which can produce a negative thumb size/position and causes drag math on tiny scroll areas to degenerate instead of scrolling; clamp the track length to zero after subtracting the corner gap.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F6F13
  db=3329545302 crates/ars-components/src/layout/scroll_area/mod.rs:724
  **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep hover leaves from cancelling active thumb drags**

In `Hover` mode, dragging a thumb outside the root commonly fires a root or scrollbar leave while the pointer is still captured; this branch transitions to `Idle` and hides the scrollbars even when `state == ThumbDragging`, leaving `drag_axis` set but causing subsequent `ThumbDragMove` events to be ignored. The hide-timeout path already guards active drags, and these hover-leave paths need the same treatment so dragging continues until `ThumbDragEnd`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
```

  "new_string": "            Event::SyncProps => {\n                let orientation = props.orientation;\n                let visibility = props.scrollbar_visibility;\n                let min_thumb = props.min_thumb_size.unwrap_or(DEFAULT_MIN_THUMB_SIZE);\n                let hide_delay = props.hide_delay;\n                let cross = props.scrollbar_cross_size.unwrap_or(0.0);\n                let dir = props.dir.unwrap_or(Direction::Ltr);\n\n                // Switching away from `Scroll` while the hide timer is running\n                // leaves `ScrollActive` and cancels the now-orphaned `AutoHide`\n                // effect, so a stale timer cannot later hide an `Always`/`Auto`\n                // scrollbar.\n                let leaving_scroll_active = *state == State::ScrollActive\n                    && visibility != ScrollbarVisibility::Scroll;\n\n                let mut plan = if leaving_scroll_active {\n                    TransitionPlan::to(State::Idle)\n                } else {\n                    TransitionPlan::new()\n                };\n\n                plan = plan.apply(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n                    ctx.orientation = orientation;\n                    ctx.scrollbar_visibility = visibility;\n                    ctx.min_thumb_size = min_thumb;\n                    ctx.hide_delay = hide_delay;\n                    ctx.scrollbar_cross_size = cross;\n                    ctx.dir = dir;\n                    ctx.update_visibility();\n                });\n\n                if leaving_scroll_active {\n                    plan = plan.cancel_effect(Effect::AutoHide);\n                }\n\n                Some(plan)\n            }"
}

    pub fn set_props(&mut self, props: M::Props) -> SendResult<M> {
        let old_props = core::mem::replace(&mut self.props, props);

        let events = M::on_props_changed(&old_props, &self.props);

        for event in events.into_iter().rev() {
            self.event_queue.push_front(event);
        }

        self.drain_queue()
    }

    /// Unmounts the service, running all active effect cleanups.
    ///
    /// After calling this, no further [`send`](Self::send) calls are valid.
    /// In debug builds, subsequent sends will panic; in release builds,
    /// they return an inert [`SendResult`].
    pub fn unmount(&mut self, active_cleanups: Vec<CleanupFn>) {
        active_cleanups
            .into_iter()
            .rev()
            .for_each(|cleanup| cleanup());

        self.event_queue.clear();

        self.unmounted = true;
    }

    /// Returns `true` after [`unmount`](Self::unmount) has been called.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn is_unmounted(&self) -> bool {
        self.unmounted
    }

    /// Creates a connect API snapshot for producing DOM attributes.
    ///
    /// The `send` closure is used by the API to wire event handlers. The returned
    /// API borrows from this service and must not outlive it.
    pub fn connect<'a>(&'a self, send: &'a dyn Fn(M::Event)) -> M::Api<'a> {
        M::connect(&self.state, &self.context, &self.props, send)
    }

    /// Re-derives context from the new state and current props via

**Pass 2 fixes:**
- **Mode-change timer leak** — `SyncProps` leaves `ScrollActive` and `cancel_effect(AutoHide)` when switching away from `Scroll`, so a stale timer can't hide an Always/Auto scrollbar.

- **Hover-leave vs drag** — `MouseLeave`/`MouseLeaveScrollbar` skip hiding while `ThumbDragging`, so a captured-pointer leave mid-drag doesn't abort the drag.

THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F6Jbj db=3329563440 crates/ars-components/src/layout/scroll_area/mod.rs:775
  **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Guard stale hide timeouts by current mode**

If an `AutoHide` timer callback is already queued when props switch from `Scroll` to `Always`/`Auto`, `SyncProps` recomputes the scrollbar as visible but a late `HideTimeout` still enters this unconditional branch and clears both visibility flags. Adapter cleanup can cancel future timer fires but cannot retract an event that was already posted, so `Always`/`Auto` scrollbars can disappear until another resize/prop sync; this handler should ignore timeouts unless the machine is still in `Scroll` visibility mode (and typically `ScrollActive`).

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F6Jbl db=3329563442 crates/ars-components/src/layout/scroll_area/mod.rs:874
  **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Hide hover scrollbars when a drag ends off-root**

In `Hover` mode, the sequence root enter → thumb drag start → root/scrollbar leave during pointer capture → thumb up reaches this non-`Scroll` branch, but it only clears `drag_axis`. The leave handlers intentionally keep the scrollbars visible while dragging and may not fire again after pointerup, so the scrollbars remain visible even though both hover flags are false; the drag-end transition needs to reapply the hover visibility rules and hide when the pointer is no longer over the root or scrollbar.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F6Jbn db=3329563444 crates/ars-components/src/layout/scroll_area/mod.rs:298
  **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recompute active hover visibility after prop changes**

When props make a new axis eligible while the user is already in an active `Hover`/`Scroll` session, this clamp-only branch cannot turn that scrollbar on. For example, start in `Hover` mode with `Vertical`, enter the root over content that overflows both axes, then update `orientation` to `Both`: `SyncProps` calls `update_visibility`, but `scrollbar_x_visible` stays false until another enter/scroll event even though the root is still hovered. Prop sync should derive visibility from the active state/hover flags instead of only preserving existing true bits.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F6Jbp db=3329563446 crates/ars-components/src/layout/scroll_area/mod.rs:563
  **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require an explicit RTL scroll convention**

This sign-based normalization cannot distinguish the positive RTL convention at `raw == 0` from the negative convention: in the existing `RtlScrollMode::Positive` helper, `0` is the far-left/inline-end position and should normalize to `max_scroll`, but this function returns `0`, making the horizontal thumb/reporting jump to the opposite edge on Safari-style positive RTL scroll containers. The adapter needs to pass a detected convention (as `ars-collections::normalize_scroll_left_rtl` does) or this function needs equivalent mode handling.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F6Jbt db=3329563450 crates/ars-components/src/layout/scroll_area/mod.rs:686
  **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep scroll events from aborting active thumb drags**

In `ScrollbarVisibility::Scroll`, a viewport `Scroll` event received while a thumb drag is active takes this branch and transitions from `ThumbDragging` back to `ScrollActive`. That can happen during a real drag when the adapter writes the computed scroll offset to the native viewport and the browser emits its normal scroll event, after which later `ThumbDragMove` events are ignored by the guard below; scroll events during a drag should update offsets without leaving the drag state.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

10	
11	/// Browser convention for RTL `scrollLeft` values.
12	///
13	/// Adapters detect the convention once at startup (e.g., by writing a
14	/// known `scrollLeft` to a hidden RTL element and reading back the sign)
15	/// and reuse the result for all subsequent normalization calls.
16	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
17	pub enum RtlScrollMode {
18	    /// Chrome, Edge, Firefox: `scrollLeft` is `0` at inline-start
19	    /// (far-right), negative toward inline-end (far-left).
20	    /// Range: `-max..0`.
21	    Negative,
22	
23	    /// Safari: `scrollLeft` is `0` at far-left (inline-end in RTL),
24	    /// positive toward far-right (inline-start).
25	    /// Range: `0..max`.
26	    Positive,
27	}
28	
29	/// Normalizes a browser's `scrollLeft` value for RTL content to a
30	/// consistent `0..max_scroll` range measured from the inline-start edge.
31	///
32	/// `mode` identifies the browser's scroll convention (see
33	/// [`RtlScrollMode`]). The adapter detects this once and passes it on
34	/// every scroll event.
35	///
36	/// For LTR content, `scrollLeft` is already `0..max` and does not need
37	/// normalization.
38	#[must_use]
39	pub fn normalize_scroll_left_rtl(
40	    raw: f64,
41	    scroll_width: f64,
42	    client_width: f64,
43	    mode: RtlScrollMode,
44	) -> f64 {
45	    // Floor at 0 to prevent clamp panic when client_width > scroll_width
46	    // (transient browser measurement or caller error).
47	    let max_scroll = (scroll_width - client_width).max(0.0);
48	
49	    match mode {
50	        RtlScrollMode::Negative => {
51	            // Chrome/Firefox: raw is -max..0. Negate to get 0..max.
52	            raw.abs().clamp(0.0, max_scroll)
53	        }
54	
55	        RtlScrollMode::Positive => {
56	            // Safari: raw is 0 (far-left / inline-end) to max (far-right /
57	            // inline-start). Convert to inline-start distance: max - raw.
58	            (max_scroll - raw).clamp(0.0, max_scroll)
59	        }
60	    }
61	}

  "new_string": "    /// Recompute scrollbar visibility after a metrics or prop change.\n    ///\n    /// `Always` and `Auto` derive visibility directly from orientation and\n    /// overflow. For `Hover`/`Scroll`, visibility tracks whether a hover/scroll\n    /// session is currently `active` (state `Hovering`/`ScrollActive`): when\n    /// active, each enabled+overflowing axis shows — so a prop/metrics change\n    /// that newly enables an axis turns it on; when inactive, both hide.\n    pub fn update_visibility(&mut self, active: bool) {\n        match self.scrollbar_visibility {\n            ScrollbarVisibility::Always | ScrollbarVisibility::Auto => {\n                self.scrollbar_x_visible = self.can_show_x();\n                self.scrollbar_y_visible = self.can_show_y();\n            }\n\n            ScrollbarVisibility::Hover | ScrollbarVisibility::Scroll => {\n                self.scrollbar_x_visible = active && self.can_show_x();\n                self.scrollbar_y_visible = active && self.can_show_y();\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Whether a `Hover`/`Scroll` session is currently active for the given state,\n/// i.e. scrollbars should be shown for eligible axes.\nconst fn is_session_active(state: &State) -> bool {\n    matches!(state, State::Hovering | State::ScrollActive)\n}"
}

546	/// Normalizes a raw `scrollLeft` value across browser RTL conventions to a
547	/// 0-to-positive range `[0, scroll_width - client_width]`.
548	///
549	/// Adapters read the live `scrollLeft` and call this before sending
550	/// [`Event::Scroll`] so the machine always works in a single convention:
551	///
552	/// - Standard (Chrome, Firefox >= 112): negative values, `0` at the left edge.
553	/// - Legacy Firefox (< 112): negative values, `0` at the right edge (handled
554	///   identically to the standard negative convention).
555	/// - Safari/WebKit: positive values, `0` at the right edge.
556	///
557	/// In LTR the raw value is returned unchanged.
558	#[must_use]
559	pub fn normalize_scroll_left(raw: f64, scroll_width: f64, client_width: f64, is_rtl: bool) -> f64 {
560	    if !is_rtl {
561	        return raw;
562	    }
563	
564	    // Modern standard: raw <= 0, normalize to a positive range.
565	    if raw <= 0.0 {
566	        raw.abs()
567	    } else {
568	        // Safari positive convention: already positive, mirror it.
569	        scroll_width - client_width - raw
570	    }
571	}

  "old_string": "    /// Recompute visibility after a metrics or prop change. `Always`/`Auto`\n    /// derive directly from orientation + overflow; `Hover`/`Scroll` are\n    /// event-driven but still clamped off for any axis the orientation disables\n    /// or that no longer overflows, so a stale scrollbar cannot linger.\n    pub fn update_visibility(&mut self) {\n        match self.scrollbar_visibility {\n            ScrollbarVisibility::Always | ScrollbarVisibility::Auto => {\n                self.scrollbar_x_visible = self.can_show_x();\n                self.scrollbar_y_visible = self.can_show_y();\n            }\n            ScrollbarVisibility::Hover | ScrollbarVisibility::Scroll => {\n                self.scrollbar_x_visible &= self.can_show_x();\n                self.scrollbar_y_visible &= self.can_show_y();\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n```",
  "new_string": "    /// Recompute visibility after a metrics or prop change. `Always`/`Auto`\n    /// derive directly from orientation + overflow. For `Hover`/`Scroll`,\n    /// visibility tracks whether a hover/scroll session is `active` (state\n    /// `Hovering`/`ScrollActive`): when active each enabled+overflowing axis\n    /// shows — so a change that newly enables an axis turns it on; when inactive\n    /// both hide.\n    pub fn update_visibility(&mut self, active: bool) {\n        match self.scrollbar_visibility {\n            ScrollbarVisibility::Always | ScrollbarVisibility::Auto => {\n                self.scrollbar_x_visible = self.can_show_x();\n                self.scrollbar_y_visible = self.can_show_y();\n            }\n            ScrollbarVisibility::Hover | ScrollbarVisibility::Scroll => {\n                self.scrollbar_x_visible = active && self.can_show_x();\n                self.scrollbar_y_visible = active && self.can_show_y();\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Whether a `Hover`/`Scroll` session is active (scrollbars should show for\n/// eligible axes) for the given state.\nconst fn is_session_active(state: &State) -> bool {\n    matches!(state, State::Hovering | State::ScrollActive)\n}\n```"
}

854	### 4.2 RTL Support
855	
856	**Vertical scrollbar position:** In `dir="rtl"`, `data-ars-dir="rtl"` is set on Root. CSS targets this to move the vertical scrollbar to the left side:
857	
858	```css
859	[data-ars-dir="rtl"] [data-ars-part="scrollbar-y"] {
860	    right: auto;
861	    left: 0;
862	}
863	```
864	
865	**Horizontal scroll normalization:** RTL browsers use different `scrollLeft` conventions. The machine normalizes to a 0-to-positive range:
866	
867	```rust
868	/// Normalizes `scrollLeft` across browser RTL conventions.
869	/// - Standard (Chrome, Firefox >= 112): negative values, 0 at left edge
870	/// - Legacy Firefox (< 112): negative values, 0 at right edge
871	/// - Safari/WebKit: positive values, 0 at right edge
872	///
873	/// Returns normalized value in range [0, scrollWidth - clientWidth].
874	///
875	/// Public because adapters call it to normalize the live `scrollLeft` read
876	/// before sending `Event::Scroll`; the machine itself always works in the
877	/// single normalized convention.
878	pub fn normalize_scroll_left(raw: f64, scroll_width: f64, client_width: f64, is_rtl: bool) -> f64 {
879	    if !is_rtl {
880	        return raw;
881	    }
882	    // Detect convention by checking sign of scrollLeft at initial position
883	    // Modern standard: raw <= 0, normalize to positive range
884	    if raw <= 0.0 {
885	        raw.abs()
886	    } else {
887	        // Safari positive convention: already positive
888	        scroll_width - client_width - raw
889	    }
890	}
891	```
892	
893	## 5. Library Parity
894	
895	> Compared against: Ark UI (`ScrollArea`), Radix UI (`ScrollArea`).
```

The machine normalizes to a 0-to-positive range:\n\n```rust\n/// Normalizes `scrollLeft` across browser RTL conventions.\n/// - Standard (Chrome, Firefox >= 112): negative values, 0 at left edge\n/// - Legacy Firefox (< 112): negative values, 0 at right edge\n/// - Safari/WebKit: positive values, 0 at right edge\n///\n/// Returns normalized value in range [0, scrollWidth - clientWidth].\n///\n/// Public because adapters call it to normalize the live `scrollLeft` read\n/// before sending `Event::Scroll`; the machine itself always works in the\n/// single normalized convention.\npub fn normalize_scroll_left(raw: f64, scroll_width: f64, client_width: f64, is_rtl: bool) -> f64 {\n    if !is_rtl {\n        return raw;\n    }\n    // Detect convention by checking sign of scrollLeft at initial position\n    // Modern standard: raw <= 0, normalize to positive range\n    if raw <= 0.0 {\n        raw.abs()\n    } else {\n        // Safari positive convention: already positive\n        scroll_width - client_width - raw\n    }\n}\n```",
  "new_string": "**Horizontal scroll normalization:** RTL browsers use different `scrollLeft`\nconventions, and the two cannot be told apart from a single sample (both report\n`0` at one edge). The adapter therefore detects the browser's convention once and\nnormalizes through the shared, convention-explicit helper from `ars-collections`\n— re-exported from this module — before sending `Event::Scroll`:\n\n```rust\npub use ars_collections::{normalize_scroll_left_rtl, RtlScrollMode};\n\n// Adapter, on each horizontal scroll event (RTL only):\nlet normalized_x = normalize_scroll_left_rtl(raw_scroll_left, scroll_width, client_width, mode);\n// `mode: RtlScrollMode` is `Negative` (Chrome/Edge/Firefox) or `Positive`\n// (Safari), detected once at startup. LTR `scrollLeft` is already `0..max` and\n// needs no normalization. The machine always works in the normalized\n// inline-start `0..max` range.\n```"
}

THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F6Nb3 db=3329583949 crates/ars-components/src/layout/scroll_area/mod.rs:808
  **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Cancel the scroll-mode hide timer when a drag starts**

When `Scroll` visibility already has an `Effect::AutoHide` timer running, starting a thumb drag should cancel it before the drag-end path starts a fresh timer. As written, if the user starts and releases a drag before the original `hide_delay` expires, the old timer can fire after `ThumbDragEnd` returns to `ScrollActive` and hide the scrollbar earlier than one full `hide_delay` after the drag. The later comment says the timer was canceled at drag start, but this plan never emits `cancel_effect(Effect::AutoHide)`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F6Nb4 db=3329583950 crates/ars-components/src/layout/scroll_area/mod.rs:704
  **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve drag state on hover re-entry**

In `Hover` mode, a `MouseEnter` event during an active thumb drag can occur when the captured pointer moves back over the root after leaving it. This branch unconditionally transitions from `ThumbDragging` to `Hovering`, so subsequent `ThumbDragMove` events are ignored by the drag-state guard and the drag stops even though the pointer is still down. The leave path already special-cases `ThumbDragging`; this enter path needs the same protection.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F6Nb6 db=3329583952 crates/ars-components/src/layout/scroll_area/mod.rs:665
  **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep resize from hiding an active drag**

When the viewport/content resizes during a thumb drag in `Hover` or `Scroll` mode, `is_session_active(State::ThumbDragging)` is false, so this resize path recomputes visibility with `active = false` and hides the scrollbar that is currently being dragged. ResizeObserver callbacks can fire during a drag (for example on window resize or content changes), and hiding the track/thumb mid-pointer-capture breaks the ongoing interaction; `ThumbDragging` needs to count as an active visibility session here.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F6Nb8 db=3329583954 crates/ars-components/src/layout/scroll_area/mod.rs:950
  **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reset hover state when visibility mode changes**

If props switch from `ScrollbarVisibility::Hover` while the machine is in `State::Hovering`, this plan keeps the old state because it only exits `ScrollActive`. After that, `MouseLeave` in `Auto`/`Always` mode only clears `hovering_root` and never transitions to `Idle`, leaving `data-ars-state="hovering"` stuck indefinitely for a component that is no longer in hover visibility mode. Treat leaving hover mode the same way as leaving scroll-active mode and reset the state.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F8cAs db=3330330947 crates/ars-components/src/layout/scroll_area/mod.rs:928
  **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clamp forward track paging to nonnegative max**

When `ScrollbarVisibility::Always` renders a scrollbar for an axis whose content does not overflow, a track click reported just past the full thumb/corner-adjusted track can take this forward-page branch; `content_size - viewport_size` is then negative, so `min(...)` stores a negative `scroll_x`/`scroll_y` in context and an adapter may try to write that invalid native scroll offset. Clamp the maximum scroll extent with `.max(0.0)` before applying the forward-page limit.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F8cAu db=3330330949 crates/ars-components/src/layout/scroll_area/mod.rs:695
  **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Implement the auto-hide effect setup**

When ScrollArea is wired through the existing adapter hooks (`use_machine` in both Leptos and Dioxus), pending effects are consumed by calling their setup closure; this closure only returns `no_cleanup()`, so a `Scroll` in `ScrollbarVisibility::Scroll` mode records a no-op effect and no timer ever sends `HideTimeout`. The visible scrollbar will therefore remain in `ScrollActive` indefinitely unless each future adapter bypasses the shared hook and reimplements effect handling; schedule the hide timer in this effect setup or expose a hook that lets adapters handle this marker before it is consumed.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F8cAv db=3330330951 crates/ars-components/src/layout/scroll_area/mod.rs:668
  **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clamp stored offsets after resize**

When the viewport or content shrinks after the user has scrolled near the old end, this resize path updates the dimensions but leaves `scroll_x`/`scroll_y` at their previous values even if they now exceed the new maximum or the axis no longer overflows. Until a later scroll event happens, APIs like `is_at_top`, `scroll_progress`, and any adapter syncing native scroll from context observe an impossible offset; clamp both stored offsets to `0..=(content - viewport).max(0.0)` after applying the new metrics.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
```

The adapter `handle_effects` calls `effect.run()` (the setup closure); the canonical `tooltip` emits delay timers as bare `PendingEffect::named(...)` markers that the **adapter component** (out of scope here) translates into timers — the agnostic core has no platform access in the setup closure and must not own timers. So cAu's "schedule the timer in core" isn't possible/in-scope; the named marker + documented §1.6.1 adapter contract is the intended split.

622	#### 1.6.1 Adapter Contract: Auto-Hide Timer
623	
624	Timers are a platform concern, so the agnostic machine never calls
625	`set_timeout`/`clear_timeout` itself. Instead, a `Scroll` event in
626	`ScrollbarVisibility::Scroll` mode transitions to `State::ScrollActive` and emits
627	the named `Effect::AutoHide` intent. The adapter is responsible for:
628	
629	1. Starting (or restarting) a timer for `Context::hide_delay` when it observes
630	   `Effect::AutoHide`.
631	2. Sending `Event::HideTimeout` back to the machine when the timer fires.
632	
633	The machine's `HideTimeout` handler then hides the scrollbars and returns to
634	`State::Idle` (unless a thumb drag is in progress). Because each new `Scroll`
635	event re-emits `Effect::AutoHide`, the adapter should treat a fresh intent as a
636	"reset the timer" signal, keeping the scrollbar visible while scrolling
637	continues.
638

  "new_string": "#### 1.6.1 Adapter Contract: Auto-Hide Timer\n\nTimers are a platform concern, so the agnostic machine never calls\n`set_timeout`/`clear_timeout` itself. `Effect::AutoHide` is emitted as a bare\n`PendingEffect::named(Effect::AutoHide)` **marker** (the same pattern Tooltip\nuses for `OpenDelay`/`CloseDelay`): its `run()` is a no-op, so the marker on its\nown schedules nothing. **The scroll-area adapter component is responsible for\ntranslating the marker into a real timer** — inspecting the emitted\n`pending_effects` for `Effect::AutoHide` rather than relying solely on the generic\n`use_machine` cleanup pass, since that pass only runs the (no-op) setup closure.\nThis split is deliberate: the agnostic core cannot reach a platform from a\ntransition, and adapter timer wiring is out of scope for the core crate (a\nseparate adapter task, exactly as for Tooltip).\n\nThe adapter must:\n\n1. Start (or restart) a timer for `Context::hide_delay` when it observes a\n   pending `Effect::AutoHide`.\n2. Send `Event::HideTimeout` back to the machine when the timer fires.\n3. Cancel the outstanding timer when it observes `Effect::AutoHide` in the\n   `cancel_effects` list (emitted on `ThumbDragStart`) or on any state change.\n\nThe machine's `HideTimeout` handler then hides the scrollbars and returns to\n`State::Idle` (only while still in `Scroll` mode and not dragging). Because each\nnew `Scroll` event re-emits the marker, the adapter treats a fresh intent as a\n\"reset the timer\" signal, keeping the scrollbar visible while scrolling\ncontinues."

> AGENT

Two of the three pass-5 findings (clamp forward paging cAs, clamp offsets after resize cAv) are clear bugs — fixed with tests. The third (cAu) is a judgment call I want your input on before resolving.

**cAu — "the AutoHide timer never fires"**: Codex correctly observes that the generic `use_machine` hook just runs the effect's (no-op) setup closure, so `Effect::AutoHide` alone schedules no timer and a `Scroll`-mode scrollbar would stay visible. Its fix options were "schedule the timer in the effect setup, or expose a hook for adapters."

My analysis: scheduling a timer in the agnostic core is impossible and out of scope — a transition's setup closure has no platform access, and the issue explicitly bars DOM/platform calls + adapter wiring from this crate. The canonical `tooltip` component handles its `OpenDelay`/`CloseDelay` identically: it emits a bare `PendingEffect::named(...)` marker that the **adapter component** (a separate, out-of-scope task) translates into a timer. I've aligned `AutoHide` to that exact `PendingEffect::named` marker and strengthened the §1.6.1 contract to spell out the adapter's timer responsibility (start/restart/cancel/send-back).

So I believe cAu is "working as designed for an agnostic core" rather than a bug — the timer lands in the adapter task, just like tooltip.

THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F8i0Z db=3330366449 crates/ars-components/src/layout/scroll_area/mod.rs:696
  **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clamp scroll offsets before storing them**

When the viewport reports a transient out-of-range offset (for example WebKit/Safari rubber-band overscroll can produce negative scroll offsets, or a stale programmatic scroll arrives after content shrinks), this path stores it verbatim. The rest of the machine assumes offsets are in `0..=max` (the resize path clamps to that range, and thumb metrics use `scroll_x`/`scroll_y` directly), so the custom thumb can be computed outside its track until another valid scroll/resize arrives. Clamp `sx`/`sy` against the current content/viewport bounds before writing them in the `Scroll` branches.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F8i0a db=3330366451 crates/ars-components/src/layout/scroll_area/mod.rs:1186
  **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Drop aria-orientation from decorative scrollbars**

When adapters render these attributes, the track gets `role="none"` while also carrying `aria-orientation`; because these custom scrollbars are intentionally decorative mirrors of the native viewport, `aria-orientation` is not valid or useful on this presentational role and can trigger ARIA allowed-attribute/a11y checks. Remove the ARIA orientation from both decorative track attr builders (or use a `data-*` marker if styling needs the axis).

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F8i0b db=3330366452 crates/ars-components/src/layout/scroll_area/mod.rs:1244
  **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Expose corner-square visibility from core attrs**

When only one axis is visible, adapters still have no direct way to know whether the decorative corner filler should be hidden: `Api` keeps `ctx` private, and this attr builder emits no `data-ars-visible` equivalent even though the spec says the corner is visible only when both scrollbars are present. An adapter rendering the `CornerSquare` part from this API will either show a stray gap whenever one scrollbar is hidden or duplicate core visibility logic; add a visibility attribute/method based on `scrollbar_x_visible && scrollbar_y_visible`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

  "new_string": "    /// Whether the content overflows the viewport vertically.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn has_overflow_y(&self) -> bool {\n        self.content_height > self.viewport_height\n    }\n\n    /// Clamp the stored scroll offsets into `0..=(content - viewport)` on each\n    /// axis. The rest of the machine (thumb metrics, edge queries) assumes\n    /// in-range offsets, so any externally-supplied value — overscroll bounce,\n    /// a stale programmatic scroll after the content shrank — is clamped before\n    /// it is stored.\n    fn clamp_offsets(&mut self) {\n        self.scroll_x = self\n            .scroll_x\n            .clamp(0.0, (self.content_width - self.viewport_width).max(0.0));\n        self.scroll_y = self\n            .scroll_y\n            .clamp(0.0, (self.content_height - self.viewport_height).max(0.0));\n    }"
}

  "new_string": "    /// Attributes for the corner gap shown when both scrollbars are present.\n    ///\n    /// `data-ars-visible` is `true` only when both scrollbars are visible, so\n    /// adapters can hide the filler when a single axis is showing without\n    /// duplicating the core visibility logic.\n    #[must_use]\n    pub fn corner_square_attrs(&self) -> AttrMap {\n        let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();\n        let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = Part::CornerSquare.data_attrs();\n\n        attrs\n            .set(scope_attr, scope_val)\n            .set(part_attr, part_val)\n            .set(HtmlAttr::Role, \"none\")\n            .set_bool(\n                HtmlAttr::Data(\"ars-visible\"),\n                self.ctx.scrollbar_x_visible && self.ctx.scrollbar_y_visible,\n            );\n\n        attrs\n    }"
}

THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F8pel db=3330401339 crates/ars-components/src/layout/scroll_area/mod.rs:683
  **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Rebase drag metrics after resize**

When a `Resize` event arrives during `State::ThumbDragging`, this block updates the viewport/content dimensions but leaves `drag_start_thumb_pos` and `drag_start_scroll_pos` captured against the old track geometry. The next `ThumbDragMove` combines the stale start thumb with the new `axis_metrics`, so a zero-delta move after a layout/ResizeObserver change can jump the scroll position (for example, `scroll_y=150` in a 100px viewport resized to 200px recomputes to 75). Recompute the drag baseline or otherwise preserve the current scroll offset when accepting resize events mid-drag.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F8pen db=3330401344 crates/ars-components/src/layout/scroll_area/mod.rs:861
  **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Invert horizontal drag delta in RTL**

For `dir=Rtl` with a horizontal scrollbar, `scroll_x` is documented as normalized to distance from inline-start (the right edge), but this physical track delta is applied with the same sign as LTR. If the user drags the horizontal thumb to the right, the pointer delta is positive even though the normalized distance from inline-start should decrease, so the viewport scrolls in the opposite direction. Flip the delta/sign for `Axis::X` when `ctx.dir == Direction::Rtl` (and keep LTR/vertical unchanged).

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6F8pep db=3330401345 spec/leptos-components/layout/scroll-area.md:23
  **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the hide-delay default in the Leptos API**

Leptos `#[prop(optional)]` parameters use `Default::default()` when omitted, so an omitted `hide_delay` here becomes `Duration::ZERO` rather than the core `Props::default()` value of 1200ms introduced in this change. When the adapter forwards that value into `scroll_area::Props`, Scroll-mode scrollbars will hide immediately for consumers who rely on defaults; make this an `Option<Duration>` or give the prop an explicit `Duration::from_millis(1200)` default.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
